## D107 An assertion named a check it never ran, and the rename had to be A/B'd on one database to prove the reds beside it were not mine

`documents: content_hash matches the raw_text it carries` read only `raw_text`: its predicate is
`NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM documents WHERE raw_text = '' OR length(raw_text) < 200)`, at
`data/seed/quality.sql:955` before and after the rename. Nothing in the row touched `content_hash`,
and adding the named check was ruled out by measurement rather than by argument: on a loaded gate
database, 0 of 1,040 stored hashes equal `encode(digest(raw_text,'sha256'),'hex')` with pgcrypto
working (`digest` returned the expected value for a known string). The generator hashes a joined
payload, not the column it ships, so the claim is unrecoverable without a reseed that would move the
committed assertion count. The row stays and the name now says what it tests: `documents: raw_text is
substantial enough to feed RAG`.

**The commit went in through the index, not the working copy.** Another stream holds eight uncommitted
citation lines in this same file — the `CollectionsController.java` line numbers it shifted by six when
it edited that controller — so a pathspec-limited commit would have swept their work into my unit and a
plain commit would have committed their text as mine. `git show HEAD:data/seed/quality.sql` plus my one
line, hashed and staged, gave a commit whose diff is exactly one line; the worktree copy was edited to
carry both changes so the next commit from that stream cannot undo mine by accident.

**Gates.** The nine-step gate could not certify this lane's numbers, and D108 says why. The rename's own
innocence is proven by an A/B on one kept database (`nexus_gate_270354_1790448961`): the text at `9591d54`
and the text at `c1e0878` return the same 214 assertions, the same 2 red rows, the same names. One
database, two shipped texts, identical verdicts — the difference between them is a string literal.

## D108 The committed repository does not pass its own seed gate: 214 assertions at HEAD, 216 only while an uncommitted migration sits on disk

Measured in a clean linked worktree at `c1e0878`, because the shared working copy had stopped being
evidence: migrations applied 6, tables 57, `qc` rows 214, and **two assertions red** —
`a door vocabulary names a column the schema has` (offender named in its own detail:
`share_links.subject_type`) and `a CHECK-bounded column is a door vocabulary too`. The gate exited 1.

The cause is a dependency nothing had written down. `infra/db/migrations/V7__share_links.sql` exists in
the working copy and has never been committed — `git log` for that path is empty — while this lane's door
vocabulary has named `share_links.subject_type` since D69 through D74 (`git log -S` on
`data/seed/quality.sql` returns `b51c043`, `6097d3b`, `99151f6`, `2d9e279`). So every number this lane
printed this session as if it were the project's — 216 checks, 58 tables, 7 migrations, and every
"x of 216 witnessed" ratio beside them — is a working-copy number, true only while another stream's
uncommitted file happens to be on disk. That is a retraction, named as one rather than edited out of the
earlier entries: the counts were real measurements of a tree that is not the committed tree.

**No code change is honest here, so none was made.** Dropping `share_links.subject_type` from the
vocabulary turns HEAD green and reddens the working copy instead, because the second assertion demands
every schema-bounded column be catalogued and the uncommitted migration is exactly what bounds it.
Committing V7 is not this lane's file. The only sound action is to say which plane a count belongs to and
to hand the decision to whoever can commit the migration — filed as a report task, with the A/B above as
its evidence. The assertion that caught it is itself witnessed in `data/seed/falsifiers.tsv` by other
arms, so it was not distrusted: it was believed.

**Six more arms, and the first witness that is a commit.** `data/seed/falsifier_plants.py` plants a
phone outside the reserved 2xxx-0000 range, a document and a fact sourced from a live URL, a merchant
image on a third-party host, a merchant page made indexable, and a user carrying a real password hash.
Each arm runs in its own `BEGIN ... ROLLBACK`, so twelve sessions share one loaded database and the last
one still sees what the loader wrote; each is paired with an unmutated control, because a plant that
reddens an assertion whose control is already red has shown nothing. All six: control green, plant red,
one row read each. The registry grows from 41 rows / 22 assertions to 47 rows / **27 of 214 (12.6%)** —
plane stated, because at HEAD the denominator is 214. The witness column now names a commit
(`111d5de`) instead of a path under a temp directory, which is the branch the validator has supported
since D103 and this lane never used: a commit cannot be swept by a disk clean-up.

**And the harness failed before it passed, in the way worth recording.** Its first run died on
`function max(boolean) does not exist` in its own reporting query, and printed `ABORTED` /
`a run read 0 rows, not 1 -- UNREAD, not green` / `RESULT: FAIL` for all twelve sessions. Zero rows read
is not a green gate; the file knew that before it produced a single verdict, which is the only reason the
first PASS is trustworthy. The check names it reports are read back out of the `qc` row the shipped
statement inserted, not retyped here — the §-bearing name
`SEO pages are noindex (demo must not rank, §155)` came through intact for exactly that reason.

**Gates.** `scripts/db_gate_fresh.sh --keep` in a clean worktree at `c1e0878`: exit 1, the two reds above,
log kept as `gate-d107-official.log` with `GATE_RC` written inside it rather than inferred from a
notification. Plants: `d107_plants.txt`, exit 0, `PLANTS_RC=0` echoed from the python process itself.
Registry validator against the same kept database: `RESULT: PASS`, 47 rows, 27 of 214.

## D109 The plants stop being single-row splices: the whole gate runs behind each one, and the biggest collateral row turns out to be a trigger

**Asked.** D108 left two things open: six arms is a small fraction of 214, and a spliced single assertion
answers only "did this predicate move". The question that matters when a row is planted is *which* rows
moved -- so the drive was changed to run the shipped gate whole inside each plant's transaction, print the
collateral, and judge an arm only on its own assertion. Seven more arms were written on producers no
earlier arm touched: a counter, a price band, a text floor, a lorem body, a coverage floor, a disclaimer
marker.

**Measured** (`data/seed/falsifier_plants.py` at `4503424`, against the kept gate database
`nexus_gate_270354_1790448961`, log `d109_final.txt` with `PLANTS_RC=0` written by the process itself):
baseline 214 assertions, red = 2, both the D108-declared pair; **13 of 13 arms reddened exactly the
assertion that names them**; 16 whole-gate sessions (the harness printed 29; D120) in one transaction each, closing baseline identical to
the opening one (that equality is how the run knows it left the data as the loader wrote it). Registry
`data/seed/falsifiers.tsv` 47 -> 54 rows; validator `RESULT: PASS`, **33 of 214 (15.4%)** assertions now
carry a machine-checkable witness. Rows and covered assertions differ by one because
`price_min <= price_max` was already filed by D105's schema-rejection arm: the registry keys on
(check, arm), and a check falsified two different ways has two witnesses.

**The collateral, and what it was.** Ten of the twelve arms reddened
`every column that cannot vary is answered for why it cannot` without being written to, which looked like
over-sensitivity in the assertion. It is not. The seed schema attaches `public.set_updated_at()` -- a
BEFORE UPDATE trigger, `NEW.updated_at = now()` -- to fifteen tables (measured through `pg_trigger` joined
on `tgfoid`, not inferred), and `spread_cat` classifies each numeric/date/timestamp column by
`count(DISTINCT)`: a column answered `single-instant-pinned` that gains a second instant is a stale
exemption, which is precisely what that row exists to notice. Two facts pin the explanation down:

  * the two arms that produced *no* collateral are the two `reviews.body` plants, and `reviews` is not one
    of the fifteen trigger tables -- its `updated_at` already holds 10,495 distinct values across 11,000
    rows, so nothing can un-pin it;
  * the control re-ran arm 0's identical plant with `SET LOCAL session_replication_role = replica`, and
    the collateral went to zero while the target stayed red. Same deception, one variable.

So the answer to D108's open question is *companion row by design*, and the drive now says so in its own
output rather than leaving a reader to chase eleven unexplained reds.

**Arm 13, stated on its own.** Having established the mechanism, the row deserves a witness that is not an
accident of another arm: the thirteenth plant moves only a timestamp
(`UPDATE merchants SET updated_at = now() ...`), reddens the spread row, and reports collateral 0. This is
the fourth case in three units where a check that was already firing as a side effect was worth promoting
to a deliberate arm (D96's window row, D105's schema backstops, D108's rename A/B, now this).

**A claim taken back -- four ledger entries that never existed.** Writing "as recorded in D103" for this
unit's context prompted a check, and `git log -S'## D103' -- docs/DECISIONS.md` returns nothing, same for
D104, D105 and D106. Those four units exist as commits (`476324d`, `9ba17f4`, `0d802be`, `9591d54`) and as
rows appended to `data/seed/falsifiers.tsv`, and as nothing else -- `git show --stat` on each lists only the
tsv (plus `scripts/check_falsifier_registry.mjs` at D103), so neither ledger holds a word about them. The habit this lane states out loud -- work commit,
then a ledger commit writing DECISIONS and STATUS -- silently stopped after D102's ledger commit, and four
units of *why* were not written down even though four units of *what* were. Nothing in the four commits is
nowhere in the tree, so this is a missing record, not a lost change; #76 is re-scoped from "STATUS lags
DECISIONS" to "DECISIONS is missing D103–D106, to be reconstructed from those commits".

**Limits of this run.** The gate body is read from the working copy, and the working copy holds another
lane's uncommitted `data/seed/quality.sql` citation edits and `infra/db/migrations/V7__share_links.sql`;
214 assertions and 2 reds are therefore the *committed-migrations / dirty-vocabulary* plane, exactly as in
D108. The drive needs a kept loaded seed (`scripts/db_gate_fresh.sh --keep`); it does not build one. And a
plant into any of the fifteen trigger tables is no longer single-dimension -- D65's rule now holds "except
for `updated_at`, which the schema writes for you", an exception that is named in the harness docstring
instead of being hidden by disabling the trigger for every arm.

## D110 A checker that crashed where it owed a verdict gets its guard committed -- with the reason and the one arm that was never witnessed written down

**What was found.** Clearing D109's retraction led to a hunk in `scripts/check_ledger_citations.mjs` that
is in neither ledger and in no commit: `ledgerText` had been rewritten to return `{text, reason}`, the
census had started collecting `unread`, and a `RESULT: UNCHECKED` block had been placed ahead of the
vacuity guards. So this lane has twice now produced an artifact whose *bytes* were in the tree and whose
*reason* was nowhere: D103-D106 left their evidence in commits and skipped both ledgers, and this hunk
skipped the commit as well. The unit below is that hunk paid for after the fact, and the defect class is
the same one D96 named for the seed gate -- a crashed reader reporting as a verdict.

**Measured, both ways, against the committed bytes.** The arm is `--text=docs/NOPE_SUCH_LEDGER.md`, the
flag D101 added so a witness does not have to write into a ledger two other lanes are appending to:

  * HEAD's version, same argv: an uncaught `Error: ENOENT ... at readFileSync` stack and exit 1
    (`d110_head_crash.txt`). Exit 1 is also what a *red* verdict exits, so a reader who did not open the
    stack could not tell "the ledgers mis-cite" from "the reader could not read".
  * The working copy's version: `RESULT: UNCHECKED -- 1 ledger read(s) failed across the 1 ledger file(s)`,
    naming the plane and the file and carrying the OS reason, exit 2 (`d110_unread_arm.txt`).
  * Controls that must stay green: HEAD-strict 212 citation-shaped tokens out of 405 `name:number` tokens,
    195 sections, working copy reported at 218 citations / 204 sections / 0 offenders, exit 0
    (`d110_ledger_head.txt`); `--worktree` 218 / 204 / 0 offenders, exit 0 (`d110_ledger_worktree.txt`).

**Widened while committing.** The unwritten hunk tested only the strict census. In the default mode the
working copy is *reported*, and a report line reading "218 in 204 section(s), 0 offender(s)" is exactly
the invention the hunk existed to refuse -- so `unread` now concatenates both planes, each entry labelled
`HEAD` or `working copy`. The reachable arm exercises the accounting path; the specific combination
"readable at HEAD, missing on disk" is **not witnessed**, because reaching it means renaming a tracked
file that two other lanes are appending to, which this lane does not do. That limit is written here rather
than left as an unwitnessed green.

**One claim in the hunk's own comment is not reproducible right now.** It says this machine refuses to
spawn `git` with `EBUSY` and that the refusal is what took the checker down. What is witnessed here is the
`ENOENT` spelling; the `git show` half is unchanged in behaviour and the guard prints whatever
`error.code` the failed read carries, so a spawn refusal and a missing file produce the same verdict text
with different reasons. The guard therefore does not distinguish "git cannot run" from "the ledger is not
in HEAD", and does not claim to.

## D111 Four units were reconstructed from their own commits -- and the re-measurable half of each claim was measured again rather than copied

**Why the insert above exists.** D109 found that D103-D106 have no decision entry anywhere, so their
*reason* survived only in four commit messages. Commit messages are evidence, but they are evidence written
on the day: they carry the number that was current then, and a backfill that only copies them would turn
four contemporaneous measurements into four unverifiable quotations. So each reconstructed entry above ends
with a bolded re-verification, and what it says is fixed by a run today rather than by memory:

  * D103's non-vacuity arm -- `node scripts/check_falsifier_registry.mjs` with no `--db` -- still prints
    `RESULT: NOT CHECKED` and exits 2. Its 22-row / 11-assertion state is *not* claimed current; the
    registry is at 54 rows / 33 of 214 since D109.
  * D104's three refusals: `reviews_rating_check` and `availability_slots_capacity_bounds` are live CHECKs
    (`convalidated = true`), and `facts_one_row_per_claim_uidx` is a UNIQUE index, not a CHECK -- a
    correction the original message did not make, because it did not need to: it was describing a refusal,
    not the shape of the object that refused. #71 is about CHECKs, so the distinction now matters.
  * D105's constraint state after its rollback: still in place, same two queries.
  * D106's second loose end is closed rather than left open, because the backfill is written after D107:
    the row was renamed in `c1e0878`. An entry written on the day would have stopped at the puzzle.

**What a backfill cannot recover.** The contemporaneous run logs stay in `nexus-d63/` (Temp) as the
registry's witnesses -- `d104_plants.py`, `d105_noconstraint.py`, `d106_plants.py` and their outputs -- and
they are only *openable*, not re-runnable to the same numbers: the assertion denominator has moved twice
since (216 -> 214 with D108's plane discovery). Re-running those drivers now would produce a different
count and would not be the witness D104 filed. The entries above therefore keep the historical number and
label the current one, in the same paragraph.

**The standing rule this unit writes down.** A unit is not closed when its artifact is committed; it is
closed when both ledgers carry it, and the check is mechanical: `git status` for an anonymous hunk in a
file this lane owns (that was D110's finding -- a guard with no commit and no entry), and
`git log -S'## Dxx' -- docs/DECISIONS.md` for an entry that never existed (D109's finding, four units).
`docs/STATUS.md` gets one section for these four units rather than four, because the working copy already
holds another lane's uncommitted sections numbered up to §108 and this lane numbers forward from there.




## D112 Seven more plants filed, one of them aimed at the wrong row — and the whole-gate run is what caught the mis-aimment — 2026-09-27

D109 left the falsifier drive running on the whole gate: one transaction per arm, the shipped
`data/seed/quality.sql` body executed inside it, `qc` read back, then rolled back. This unit added arms
chosen from a computed queue and found, on the first attempt, that the drive can now tell the difference
between *the data is fine* and *the plant does not reach the row it claims to reach*.

**The queue was computed, not remembered.** Before writing any SQL, the unwitnessed names were read off
`qc` on the kept gate database and filtered (`names read off qc 214`, distinct 214; `registry check names`
33 at that moment; names built at run time by the D98 sweeps — the `fk:`/`orphan:`/`shape:`/`volume:` and
similar prefixes — excluded, leaving **109 literal-named** assertions; of those, 28 already witnessed and
**81 without a witness**). The script and its dump live in the machine's Temp directory
(`nexus-d63/queue.py`, `names_all.txt`, `d112_queue.txt`), not in the repository, so those four numbers are
a reading of one plane at one moment — 214 is the committed-HEAD count, and D108's warning still holds:
with another stream's uncommitted `infra/db/migrations/V7__share_links.sql` on disk the same gate files 216.
What is durable is the recipe: slice `quality.sql` at its own hard-gate marker, run it in the same session
`qc` belongs to (`qc` is a TEMP table, so a fresh psql cannot list it), aggregate the names out in one row.

**Every column a plant touches was checked against `pg_attribute` first.** That is the direct product of
D106, whose plant wrote `UPDATE documents SET text = ...` when the column is `raw_text` — and the harness
reported it as *an unread arm* instead of letting a psql error look like a green one. This batch's seven SQL statements were written only after the columns were confirmed
(`documents.raw_text`, `chunks.token_count`, `chunks.ordinal`, `chunks.document_id`, `categories.parent_id`,
`merchants.category_primary`, `facts.value`), and `merchants.data_origin` was additionally checked for
schema bounds: `pg_constraint` lateral-joined on `conkey` returns **no CHECK on the `data_origin` column of
any of the three tables that carry it** (`collections`, `merchants`, `reviews` — all plain `text`). The
schema will not refuse the deception, which is exactly why the assertion has to be the thing that catches
it — the same shape of finding D105 recorded for the three arms the schema *did* refuse, read from the
other side.

**The arm that did not land.** The first version of the seventh arm planted
`UPDATE facts SET value = jsonb_set(value, '{data_origin}', '"human"'::jsonb)` and claimed the assertion
`data_origin = demo everywhere the column exists`. The run reported it as `green` with four reddened rows
besides it, and `RESULT: FAIL`. Reading the claimed row: it predicates `data_origin <> 'demo'` over the
three **plain columns** (`merchants`, `reviews`, `collections`) and nothing else — it cannot see a jsonb
key of the same name, so a fact payload stamped `human` leaves it truthfully green. Whole-gate mode is what
made that diagnosable rather than merely red: the four collateral names are the report of where the
deception actually landed (`the synthetic stamp says demo, or true, on every row of every column that
carries it`, `the §19 provenance axis and the §109 stamp axis stay separate on facts`, plus D83's spread
and clock rows). A run that executes only the claimed assertion would have said "target stayed green" and
left the reader to guess.

**Split into two arms, one per plane.** The batch now ships both: the jsonb plant claims
`the §19 provenance axis and the §109 stamp axis stay separate on facts` (collateral 3), and a plain-column
plant — `UPDATE merchants SET data_origin = 'human'` — claims `data_origin = demo everywhere the column
exists` (collateral 1, the trigger row). The two arms together establish a layering claim that neither
could make alone: **each row watches exactly one plane.** Under the jsonb plant the plain-column row stayed
green; under the plain-column plant both jsonb rows stayed green. The mechanism is readable in the shipped
file: `marker_cat`'s build loop (`DO $d80$`) iterates columns whose predicate is `t.typname = 'jsonb'` and
keys matching `origin|synth|demo|generat`, so a plain `text` column named `data_origin` is not in its
universe at all, while the 558 row reads only the three named plain columns. Neither row is a redundant
copy of the other and neither can substitute for it — which is worth stating because "two assertions about
data_origin" looks like duplication until someone plants each plane.

**Zero-collateral arms confirm D83's mechanism a second time.** Six of the twenty arms produced no
collateral. Five plant into `reviews`, `chunks` and `categories` — and those are precisely the three tables
in this batch that are not among the fifteen carrying `set_updated_at()`, so nothing but the claimed column
moves. The sixth is the arm whose target *is* the spread row (`UPDATE merchants SET updated_at = now()`),
which absorbs by definition what the other merchant-table arms show as collateral. Measured over twenty
arms rather than the twelve D109 saw, the collateral pattern tracks the trigger set with no exception in
either direction.

**A claim taken back.** D109's entry introduces the collateral as though the mechanism were found by that
unit's measurement ("which looked like over-sensitivity in the assertion. It is not. The seed schema
attaches `public.set_updated_at()`…"). It was not new. `grep -n set_updated_at docs/DECISIONS.md` puts the
same mechanism in **D83** (2026-09-25) — *an `UPDATE offerings SET min_party_size = 2` moved
`offerings.updated_at` as well, because V1:961-970 installs `set_updated_at()` as a BEFORE UPDATE trigger
on every table with that column, so the census found `offerings.updated_at` varying and refused its
`single-instant-pinned` answer. A plant that reaches a column under audit through a trigger is a plant that
cannot be undone* — and D86 (2026-09-26) states the corollary actually used by the plants, that `reviews`
carries no such trigger and therefore leaves no clock residue. What D109 legitimately added on top of that
is the fifteen-table count read through `pg_trigger` rather than inferred from the migration text, and the
reverse control (`SET LOCAL session_replication_role = replica` → collateral 0, target still red). The
lesson is the one this lane keeps re-learning and keeps failing to apply: **grep this lane's own ledger
before writing "measured, not inferred"**, because a claim of novelty about something the ledger already
records is a false citation, and D88/D87's machinery exists precisely to catch those.

**Measured** (`data/seed/falsifier_plants.py` at `975e0a5`, against `nexus_gate_270354_1790448961`; log
`d112b_plants.txt`, whose `RESULT: PASS` and 43-session count are the process's own output): opening
baseline 214 assertions with red = 2, both the D108-declared door-vocabulary pair; **20 of 20 arms reddened
exactly the assertion that names them**, no arm found an undeclared red, the control re-ran arm 0 with the
triggers off and got `target RED · collateral 0 · spread row gone`, and the closing baseline is identical
to the opening one. `data/seed/falsifiers.tsv` 54 → **61 rows** at `2c27dbe`; the validator
(`node scripts/check_falsifier_registry.mjs --db nexus_gate_270354_1790448961`) reports `RESULT: PASS` and
**40 of 214 (18.7%)** assertions carrying a machine-checkable witness. The queue recomputed from the same
214-name dump after the batch: 109 literal-named, **35 witnessed, 74 still without a witness** — seven
fewer than before, because all seven new names were unwitnessed ones.

**What the batch did not buy.** All seven new rows point their witness at `975e0a5`, the commit that
contains the arms themselves, so they are reproducible by anyone who can check out the repository and
build a seed. That is not true of the registry's older half: counted over the shipped file, **22 rows carry
a commit witness and 39 carry a path witness**, those 39 spread over 12 files under `nexus-d63/` in this
machine's Temp directory (`d99_sweep_plant.py`, `d100_three_sweeps.py`, `d104_plants.py`,
`d105_noconstraint.py`, `d106_plants.py`, and seven log excerpts). The validator accepts both forms, so the
registry reads PASS today and would read `witness cannot be opened` for 39 rows the moment the Temp
directory is cleared — a witness that only opens on the machine that wrote it is an anecdote with a
filename. Recorded as the next unit's problem, not solved here.

## D113 A witness you can only open on the machine that wrote it is an anecdote with a filename — so 39 of the registry's 61 rows moved into the repository, and the checker now refuses a path it cannot resolve from a clean checkout — 2026-09-27

D112 closed by recording that the registry's older half was not durable. This unit measures how untrue
"an artifact that still opens" was, fixes the grammar, and shows the fix on both sides.

**The defect, measured before touching anything.** The shipped checker resolved a non-sha witness under
`process.env.TMPDIR || C:/Users/18414/AppData/Local/Temp`, so 39 rows pointed at `nexus-d63/…` — five one-off
harness scripts (`d99_sweep_plant.py`, `d100_three_sweeps.py`, `d104_plants.py`, `d105_noconstraint.py`,
`d106_plants.py`) and seven run excerpts (`w5_none.txt`, `w5_load.txt`, `w5_basedate.txt`, `w5_past.txt`,
`w_d_nostamp.txt`, `w_l_d92.txt`, `w_h_plants.txt`). Two independent readings agree on the count: a column
scan of the file (61 rows = 22 commit witnesses + 39 path witnesses over 12 distinct files), and the checker
itself run with `TMPDIR` pointed at an empty directory, which reported `witness cannot be opened` for exactly
**39** rows and exited 1 while leaving the other 22 rows untouched. The green `RESULT: PASS` the registry had
been printing was therefore a property of this laptop's temp folder, not of the repository — the same class of
"measured on a tree that is not the committed tree" that D108 recorded for the assertion count, one level
further down.

**The move.** All twelve artifacts are copied into `data/seed/falsifier_witnesses/` under their original
filenames, so every prose citation to `w5_none.txt` or `d104_plants.py` in DECISIONS and STATUS still resolves.
A copy is only a witness if it is the same bytes, so each of the twelve was compared against the Temp original
by `md5sum`: twelve of twelve identical, no file differing. Before copying, the artifacts were scanned for
credentials and encoded blobs (`sk-…`, `password=`, `api_key`, `BEGIN RSA`, 40+ base64-ish runs, `C:/Users/…`
machine paths): the only hits are gate report lines and column names such as `fk: api_keys.merchant_id`, which
is a table name, not a key. Total added: 856 lines / ~92 KB (the twelve files as staged: 60+44+75+37+98+21+20
+19+21+379+41+41).

**The narrowed grammar** (`scripts/check_falsifier_registry.mjs`, committed at `3d237f8`): a witness is either
a commit that resolves (`git cat-file -e <sha>^{commit}`) or a path that is a **blob tracked at HEAD**
(`git cat-file -t HEAD:<path>` == `blob`). The temporary-directory branch is gone rather than kept as a
fallback — a rule with an escape hatch in the same expression is how a guard ends up decorative. HEAD
specifically, not "any commit", because what a stranger can check out is HEAD: a witness that exists only in
some unreachable object is the same failure one step earlier.

**The refusal says which state it found**, because "the file is right there and the registry is still wrong"
is a distinction this lane has already been burned by (D110's anonymous working-copy hunk). Four states, four
messages: outside the repository, tracked at HEAD as a non-blob, present in the working copy but untracked,
nowhere.

**Both sides, without dirtying the shipped data.** `--registry <path>` was added so the refusals could be
planted in scratch copies of the file instead of by editing `data/seed/falsifiers.tsv` — a guard demonstrated
by temporarily corrupting the artifact it guards also risks leaving the corruption behind, and D109's rule is
that a new validator's first run must not be its own test. Five runs against the live gate assertions
(`nexus_gate_270354_1790448961`), every one with `TMPDIR` pointed at an empty directory so nothing could hide
in the Temp folder:

  * **shipped registry (must stay green)** — `RESULT: PASS`, `22 commit(s) · 39 file(s) tracked at HEAD`.
    This is the claim that matters: the registry now validates on a machine whose temp directory is empty.
  * witness `data/seed/falsifier_witnesses/does_not_exist.txt` — FAIL, "is nowhere — neither in the repository
    nor at HEAD", kinds drop to 38.
  * witness `../outside_the_repository.txt` — FAIL, "names a path outside the repository".
  * witness `data/seed/falsifier_witnesses` (the directory) — FAIL, "is tracked at HEAD as a tree, not a file".
  * witness `scripts/list_routes.js` (another stream's untracked helper, present on disk) — FAIL, "exists in
    the working copy but is not tracked at HEAD". This is the row a lazy rule would have waved through, because
    the file *does* open.

**A claim corrected in the same diff.** The registry's own header comment opened with "The gate has 216
assertions". That is the other plane: the committed tree files 214 (D108), and 216 appears only while another
stream's uncommitted `infra/db/migrations/V7__share_links.sql` sits on disk. The header now says which plane a
percentage is taken over, because the file's headline number — 40 of 214 — is computed against `qc`, and a
reader comparing it to a run on a dirty tree would otherwise conclude the checker was wrong.

**Limits, stated.** Durability is not reproducibility. The seven `.txt` excerpts witness runs that happened
before this migration and cannot be re-executed; the five `.py` harnesses are re-runnable in principle but were
written against the gate as of D99-D106, and re-running them was not attempted here. What the unit does
guarantee is narrower and checkable: anyone with a clean checkout can open every one of the 61 witnesses, and
the checker's verdict is now a function of the repository plus a loaded seed — not of one user's temp
directory. Coverage is unchanged by design: **40 of 214 (18.7%)**, 61 rows; this unit bought the number's
meaning, not its size.

## D114 Five standing cross-stream reports re-verified: one still true as written, one fixed but uncommitted, one contradicted by its own newest artifact, one whose claim was simply wrong, and one about a file that does not exist at HEAD — 2026-09-27

This lane keeps a list of defects belonging to other streams, which it may report and must not edit. Reports
about someone else's files decay faster than reports about the seed, because their plane moves underneath them.
Five were re-read against current HEAD (`f077afa`) and the working copy, and three of the five changed state.
Nothing here edits another stream's file.

**1. The double-encoded `events.properties` write (#62) — still true, and it takes two committed layers to
make.** `apps/ai/nexus_ai/api/runs.py` builds the INSERT with `$10::jsonb, $11::jsonb` and binds
`json.dumps(event.get("properties") or {}, ensure_ascii=False)` (lines 158-159 of the working copy), while
`apps/ai/nexus_ai/db/pool.py:64` registers `encoder=json.dumps` for `jsonb`/`json` on every connection. Either
one alone would be correct; together they store a JSON *string* in a jsonb column, which is the payload-shape
plane D86 counted from the other end. The aggravating fact is trackedness, not encoding:
`git ls-files apps/ai/nexus_ai/api/` returns **0 files** — the writer is untracked, so the defect cannot be
seen from a clean checkout at all, and pool.py's `M` state means the codec's *surroundings* are also moving.
Report: pick one encoder. The committed codec is the one that also protects every other insert, so the
`json.dumps` call in the writer is the half to drop.

**2. `Guide.body_blocks` (#64) — true at HEAD, already fixed in the working copy by its owner.** At HEAD the
web type requires the field (`apps/web/src/lib/types.ts:261`, no `?`) and the platform's

the string. On disk the same file emits it (`out.put("body_blocks", bodyBlocks(items))`, working-copy line 188)
and `CollectionsReadTest` asserts it, so the drift is closed as uncommitted work. The live residue is
documentation: `grep -n body_blocks docs/API_CONTRACT.md` is 0 hits on disk **and** 0 at HEAD, so a field the

**3. `CommerceApiTest` (#58) — the report needs downgrading, not closing.** The package is still untracked
(`git ls-files services/platform/src/test/java/com/nexus/commerce` → 0 files, while the `.java` is on disk; the

**4. The worktree `docs/STATUS.md` claim (#68) — wrong, and it is this lane's own claim, so it is retracted by

file, with the same heading text as the one copy HEAD carries. Nothing on disk can
distinguish "the other stream restored it" from "it was never missing", and the 165 = 89 + 76 arithmetic D89 was

**The generalisation, stated as a rule for this lane.** A cross-stream report must carry its plane in its own
sentence — *at HEAD*, *in the working copy of a file its owner has not committed*, or *in a run whose artifact is

stream saves. Two of the five above would have stayed correct for a week longer if they had been written that

**Witnesses.** Every number above is from a read-only command re-run for this entry: `git ls-files`, `git
ls-tree HEAD`, `git show HEAD:<path> | grep -c`, `grep -rn body_blocks` over `services/platform/src`, `apps/web/src`
and `docs/API_CONTRACT.md`, the surefire XML's own attributes, and `grep -n "^## 85\|^## 100"` against both copies

## D115 A recovery commit is not a purely additive one: nine sections stranded by this lane's own staging technique come back as §115–§123, and what it cost to put them in — 2026-09-27

**Question.** D114 found that eight STATUS sections — nine including the one that records the finding —
live in `docs/STATUS.md`'s working copy and nowhere in any commit, and named the mechanism without
naming the owner. This unit asks the owner's question first: what exactly did this lane's staging
technique strand, and what does putting it back cost in lines that are not additions?

**The mechanism, stated as a rule rather than an accident.** A commit built from
`git show HEAD:docs/STATUS.md` plus one appended section cannot rescue a section that never got staged,
by construction. The technique was introduced to avoid a worse error — committing the worktree copy of a
file that holds another lane's uncommitted edits deletes theirs — and it has that property in both
directions: it never picks up what it did not write, and what it did not pick up stays unpicked up
forever. §109's and §111's own sentences explain numbering choices by reference to the uncommitted
sections; four later units read those sentences and did nothing about the sections themselves. D111 paid
this debt for `docs/DECISIONS.md` (D103–D106, reconstructed from commits) and, at the time, for STATUS —
and the same omission then recurred for the working copy, which no `git log -S` can reach because those
lines were never in any commit at all.

**What was on disk, measured before the splice.**

```
docs/STATUS.md   HEAD before the recovery  5,599 lines · 82 numbered sections · 107 `## ` headings
                 the working copy that day  6,180 lines · 116 `## ` headings  (= HEAD + 603 − 22 by
                 `git diff --numstat`, i.e. 581 net lines more, of which 562 are the nine stranded ones)
                 §100 appears twice: the working copy's route-ledger section at 5350, HEAD's D108 plane
                 correction at 5912 — a duplicate number inside one file, not two files disagreeing
                 the two planes differ in 13 further places, all of them small: §81/§84 residue lines and
                 the §85–§100 `next` blocks, where the merge lane had replaced this lane's
                 "Carried: … #68 …" lines with annotated versions that call #68 closed
docs/DECISIONS.md  clean against HEAD — no worktree-only content
                     one line of the stranded block (worktree 5910, §108's closing fence) ends CRLF;
                     every other line of the file is LF
```

The working copy's own line count is derived, not re-measured: `99e5b0c` moved HEAD from 5,599 to 6,196
lines, and the file the splice read was that result minus the 12-line recovery note, the 3 restored blank
lines and the 1 line the first gloss added — 6,180, which is HEAD-before plus the 581 net lines
`git diff --numstat` printed against it before it was overwritten. Every other number in this entry was
printed by a command run for it.

**The numbering decision, and the rule it followed.** The incoming sections move, not HEAD's. That is
§108's own precedent, stated there as "HEAD's numbers are cited by DECISIONS, from their own `next`
blocks and from later sections; the draft's numbers were cited by its own sections", and it is the
asymmetry that matters: a committed number has dependents, an uncommitted one has only its siblings. So
working-copy §100→§115 … §108→§123, chosen above HEAD's max of §114 so no committed section changes
number, and the `## 100` collision dissolves instead of being adjudicated. Each recovered title keeps its
body verbatim and carries `[recovered by D115 from the working copy's §NNN]` in its heading, so the
number the section was is on the page next to the number it is.

**References: two kinds, treated differently.** Fifteen references inside the block point a reader at a
*sibling recovered section*; those were re-aimed at the new numbers (§101→§116, §102→§117, §103→§118,
§100→§115, §106→§121, §107→§122, §108→§123), each replacement asserted to match exactly once, so a
second or absent match stops the build rather than silently mapping the wrong text. Eight other
references are *statements about a numbering event* — §123's body is a record of the earlier merge, and
lines like "§34→§100, §35→§101 …" and "max §108 · duplicate numbers none" report what happened, not where
to read. Rewriting those would have destroyed the record to protect the citation, and §108 itself is the
section that warns against exactly that ("a cross-reference that is wrong in the source is wrong after a
renumber, and renumbering is the only step that would have hidden it"). They stay verbatim, and the
recovery note ends §123 with the pair table that resolves them — added in the ledger commit rather than
the recovery commit, because the re-measurement below is what showed the cost. Two of this lane's own
committed sentences that pointed at the old working-copy numbering (§109's "numbered 109 and not 101"
paragraph, §111's "uncommitted sections up to §108") carry a dated inline gloss for the same reason.

**What a recovery commit costs.** `99e5b0c` is 618 insertions and **21 deletions**, and a ledger whose
house rule is "append" should not let that pass without a name. All 21 are lines this lane wrote: 19 of
them are §81/§84's residue text and §85–§100's `next` "(b) Carried: … #68 …" lines, each replaced by the
merge lane's annotated version of the same sentence; the other two are the two sentences this unit
glossed. No line authored by another lane is deleted, and no line of the stranded block is dropped — its
562 lines are in the file, plus the note and §124. The three blank lines the working copy had lost at the
§112/§113/§114 seams (this lane's own appending, again) were restored; three older headings (§64–§66, at
lines 2830/2873/2917) sit without a preceding blank line in HEAD itself and are named rather than
