## D116 The ledger's two planes are now compared by a step of the gate, because §123 recorded the fork three times and nobody wrote the check — 2026-09-27

**Context.** Task #68 has been open since §86 (e) found it at 08:09 on 2026-09-26, and it was written up
twice more after that: §123 (the working copy merged instead of committed, eight sections under eight
numbers committed sections already held) and D115 (nine sections committed nowhere, three days stranded,
the `## 100` collision dissolved by renumbering the incoming nine as §115–§123). Every one of those
accounts ends in the same confession: the loss was detectable by a mechanical comparison of two files,
and the mechanical comparison did not exist. D115's own `next` block named it as the thing to write, and
wrote the guard's absence as the reason to distrust every future "nothing is lost" claim.

**Decision.** Ship `scripts/check_ledger_sections.mjs` as gate step 10 of 10, with an asymmetric verdict:

- **HARD** (exit 1) — a numbered heading present at HEAD but absent from the file on disk, or a number
  claimed twice on disk. Both are the class that deletes committed history when someone commits the tree
  as it stands, which is what §123 measured: STATUS on disk was 4,598 lines against HEAD's 5,327.
- **NAMED, allowed** (exit 0) — a heading on disk and not at HEAD. That is what the middle of writing an
  entry looks like, and refusing it would refuse this lane's own staging technique, which is the only
  reason DECISIONS has ever grown. It is printed with its numbers anyway, because D115's nine sat in that
  state for three days and a name is what makes the state visible.
- **NOT CHECKED** (exit 2) — `git show` cannot spawn, a ledger is unreadable, or the heading pattern
  matches nothing. D96's answer to its own question: a reader that saw no headings did not check the
  headings, and an empty set is exactly what a renamed house convention looks like from here.

**Rejected, with the reason it was rejected.** A check over `§N` *citations* — "every §NNN in the ledgers
must resolve to a heading." It was the obvious generalisation of #79, and it is unwritable. Counted over
HEAD's two files as they stand: **1,100 `§N` tokens across 115 distinct numbers, of which 572 resolve to a
STATUS heading and 528 do not** — 381 of those are ≤ §20 (contract sections; `§8` alone appears 88 times),
42 are above §124 (`AGENT_CONTRACT` spec items, which run to §171), and 105 are numbers that are gaps in
STATUS's own sequence (§32, §80, §101–§108). §124 carried the same measurement on its own plane (958
tokens / 475 non-resolving, counted over the `99e5b0c` blob before this section's and §124's text added
their share); the two pairs differ by the text written after the counting, which is why each carries its
plane. A gate that reddens on 528 of them is not a gate. So citations stay the business of step 8/9
(`check_ledger_citations.mjs`, which resolves `File.ext:NNN` and says what it cannot), and #68's narrower,
fully mechanical question — heading at HEAD, heading on disk — is what gets a witness.

The 105 gap-tokens are not free, though, and D116 measures them rather than filing them: 81 survive once
the nine `[recovered by D115 from the working copy's §NNN]` title brackets and `§101-§108` range spellings
are excluded (28 written by §123 itself, 16 by D115, 10 by §124, the rest by older sections). §124's claim
that D115 re-aimed 15 references was true of the references *it* edited; it never claimed the residue was
zero, and it is not. Widening the guard to that residue is a content decision about 81 sentences, not a
flag — so it goes to #80, with the count attached.

**Witness.** `scripts/falsify_ledger_sections.mjs`: eight arms, each running the *shipped* checker as a
subprocess against its own fixture directory, so no arm can redden another.

```
node scripts/falsify_ledger_sections.mjs
  held  exit 0  control: this tree as it stands
  held  exit 1  a committed section deleted from the working copy
  held  exit 1  the same section duplicated on disk            (on disk: 124×2)
  held  exit 0  a draft section on disk, not yet committed     (the NAMED arm)
  held  exit 1  the DECISIONS plane, same rule
  held  exit 2  a ledger whose heading pattern matches nothing
  held  exit 2  a HEAD revision that does not resolve
  held  exit 1  the working copy D115 recovered (rebuilt: 9 headings put back as §100–§108,
                8 of them new to 99e5b0c^)
  8 arms · 8 held · 0 missed
```

The last arm is the one worth the decision. It does not assert a synthetic deletion; it **reconstructs the
real 2026-09-26 working copy from two commits** (`99e5b0c^`'s file, with the nine recovered sections
de-bracketed and re-inserted under the numbers they were written with) and predicts, from D115's own
measured properties, the three things the checker would say about it: a duplicated `100×2`, eight
disk-only, and nothing committed missing. It is a guard shown red on the tree that motivated it, and the
reconstruction lives in the repository rather than in Temp — so the next person can re-run it without
believing this entry. (D113's rule, applied to my own harness for once.)

**Both sides of the gate step, run inside the gate.** Not only inside the harness:

```
scripts/db_gate_fresh.sh                              steps 1–10 all print · step 10 PASS (92/92, 103/103)
                                                      RESULT: PASS — 216 quality checks … GATE_EXIT=0
LEDGER_SECTIONS_DIR=<fixture> bash scripts/db_gate_fresh.sh --skip-generate
                                          steps 1–9 unchanged, step 10 prints
                                            FORK docs/STATUS.md: 1 section(s) committed at HEAD and absent
                                              from the working copy — … : 124
                                          GATE_EXIT=1 — the gate dies at step 10, as a gate should
```

and the fact that the second run left **no** database behind: `pg_database` counts 2 `nexus_gate*` rows,
both from `--keep` runs, none from the failed one. §103's caution ("the gate drops its database when the
run finishes, and a run killed from outside does not get to") is confirmed on the branch it had not tested
— a nonzero step is not an external kill, and the trap fires.

**The knob, and what it is for.** `LEDGER_SECTIONS_DIR=<dir>` points step 10 at another checkout. It
exists so the in-gate red arm is reachable at all: without it the only way to show step 10 failing inside
the gate is to delete a committed section from the real tree, which is the destructive act the check
guards against. Its demonstrated use is the falsifier and the red run in §125; nothing in CI sets it.

**Residue, stated rather than implied.** Step 10 fires when someone runs `db_gate_fresh.sh`. It does not
fire on a working copy that is never gated, and it is not in `.github/workflows/ci.yml` — that file belongs
to another stream (the frozen list), so the CI arm is a report, not an edit. The gap the check does not
cover is the mirror of the HARD case: a section that exists at HEAD, on disk, and is *changed in place*
into different text is not a fork and cannot be caught this way — D115 met that one as a renumbering
question, and it stays a review question.

## D117 A bare `§NN` is three planes and a spelled one is one, so only the spelled form gets judged — and the retention citations turn out to be off by six requirement rows — 2026-09-27

**Context.** D116 shipped the heading guard and refused, with numbers, a citation gate: 1,100 `§N` tokens
in the two ledgers, 528 non-resolving, across three planes. §79 was still open as "two Java comments cite
`STATUS §106`, which resolves to nothing (means §121)". Writing the smallest mechanical version of the
refused idea — *the tokens that name their own plane* — turned out to be writable, and chasing what those
two tokens meant turned out to be the larger finding.

**What `§NN` actually is in this repository, measured.** `docs/TRACEABILITY.md:1` says it outright:
"§ numbering = `新建 文本文档.txt`" — the file is a requirement matrix whose rows are numbered §0…§171, and
that matrix, not the contract documents, is the plane the source comments overwhelmingly cite (614 `§N`
tokens in 134 Java files; §100–§171 appear there routinely). Against that matrix:

```
TRACEABILITY.md:86   | 100 | Privacy: export/delete/reset; merchant data ownership | /me/export,
                     deletion_requests | api | todo |
TRACEABILITY.md:92   | 106 | AI transparency: show why, show uncertainty | MatchExplanations,
                     degraded badge | visual | building |
```

**The finding, stated as a defect report and not as a fix.** Nine bare `§106` citations in the identity
lane describe the deletion/retention workflow: `IdentityRepository.java:106/339/360`,
`MeController.java:33/111/122/125`, `ConfigDecorationTest.java:27/52`. Their subject is row **§100**, not
row §106 — §106 is the AI-transparency row. The same off-by-six is in the design docs, which are on the
frozen list and so are reported rather than edited: `DATABASE.md:191` ("`deletion_requests` — §106
data-retention workflow"), `API_CONTRACT.md:193` (the `DELETE /api/v1/me` row, "creates
`deletion_request` (§106)"), `CONSUMER.md:59` and `SECURITY.md:57` ("Privacy & data rights (§106)").
Two consequences worth naming: the matrix says §100's verification is `api` and its status `todo`, so the
code comment at `MeController.java:122` tells a caller about a retention job whose requirement row is
officially unimplemented — which this ledger has said since §41 — and every reader who follows the §106
pointer lands on a row about model uncertainty instead.

**Decision.** `scripts/check_status_citations.mjs` judges only `STATUS §NN`, the one grammar that names its
plane, and splits citation from mention mechanically: outside a backtick span the token is a pointer a
reader follows and must be a `## N. ` heading at HEAD; inside one it is a quotation of the string and is
counted and printed but not judged. That second half is not a convenience — six spelled tokens in the
repository are the ledgers reporting the defect (§123 twice, §124 twice, §125 once, D115 once), each of
them writing `STATUS §106` precisely to name it, so a checker that judged quotations would make the
reporting of a defect a defect, and the exemption is therefore witnessed by its own arm rather than
assumed.

**Rejected.**
- *Wiring it as gate step 11 today.* Its first run on the real tree is red with two offenders that belong
  to another lane's committed files. A step that reddens a gate nobody can fix teaches people to run the
  gate with the step disabled. It ships unwired, and the wiring is conditional on #79 closing — the same
  order D102 used for the jsonb scanner (report first, gate when the tree can be green).
- *A sweep of §106 → §121 across the source.* That was §124's plan and it is wrong: it would have
  rewritten nine comments that are on the requirement-matrix plane (albeit citing the wrong row) into the
  ledger plane, replacing one defect with another. The two files that spell `STATUS` need §121; the bare
  ones need `TRACEABILITY §100`.
- *A hand list of exempted lines.* Every exemption list this project has shipped (D84's 10-name vendor
  list, §84's 14-name directory list) is documented as a residue that has to be kept current by hand. The
  backtick rule is a grammar, and grammars do not need maintaining.

**Witness.** `scripts/falsify_status_citations.mjs` — 6 arms, 6 held, over the shipped checker as a
subprocess with its own fixture directory: this tree (exit 1, both Java files named by path and line), the
fix §79 asks for (both comments rewritten to §121 → exit 0), a citation to §99999 (exit 1), the identical
token inside backticks (exit 0 as a mention, which is the arm that proves the exemption is real), a tree
with no spelled token (exit 2, D79's silence-is-not-green), an unresolvable `--head-rev` (exit 2).

**The lesson this unit caught twice, having been told it once.** The control arm of that harness first
pinned this tree's counts — `citations 4 · mentions 8` — and went MISS when the harness itself was written,
because the census walks `scripts/*.mjs` and the harness contains the string it tests. It is D116's addendum
in new clothes: an arm whose fixture is the current tree is a claim about today, and any count it pins is a
date. The control arm now asserts only the two offender lines, which are other lanes' committed files, and
it will go green exactly when #79 closes.

**Residue.** Bare `§NN` in the ledgers still has three possible planes and no mechanical resolver; D116's
81-token surface and its event-record/content-pointer split stand as #80. This unit re-aimed 6 of them —
§41–§45's bare `§106` retention citations — to `TRACEABILITY §100`, so §125 found (d)'s "6 tokens" is now
a then-statement about text this unit changed; the sentence is left verbatim for the reason D115 established
(a section that records a measurement is an event, not a pointer).

## D118 Six plants that move a number, and the discovery that the record of shown redness had never been executed by anything — 2026-09-27

**Context.** #73 asks which of the gate's assertions have been *shown* able to fail, and D113 made that a
file with a checker. The count was 40 witnessed of 216 on this plane. Twenty plant arms existed, and every
one of them fabricated something textual: a URL where `demo://` belongs, a stamp that says `human`, a name
on a blocklist, a body shortened below a floor. The gate's other half — the numeric doors, bounds and TTLs
and ratios and joins — had been watched only while the data obeyed it. Reaching for those arms is what this
unit did, and running them required reading the registry's own validator, which is where the larger finding
sat.

**Decision (a): plant on the value plane, and measure legality before aiming.** Six arms joined
`data/seed/falsifier_plants.py`, committed as d680d24: a merchant popularity score at 1.4 against a
declared `[0,1]`, a price fact stamped with the *hours* TTL instead of the six-hour one, the stale marking
cleared so the UI would never show 已過時, 2,500 Cantonese reviews relabelled English to drop the mix below
its 50% floor, a grant filed by an operator id no user holds, and a merchant renamed to a real chain from
the §109 blocklist. Each was probed against `pg_constraint` first, because a plant the schema refuses is
evidence about the schema, not the assertion: none of those five columns carries a CHECK, so all five
deceptions reach the gate alive, and the assertions that catch them are the last line rather than a
backstop. The drive ran 26 arms plus the trigger control across 29 whole-gate sessions (printed 55; D120) on one kept loaded
database: baseline 216 assertions red 0, every arm's own assertion RED, collateral 1/2/2/0/0/1 with every
line of it one of the two known `updated_at`-spread rows, closing baseline identical to opening, exit 0 —
and the rows entered `data/seed/falsifiers.tsv` only from that drive's own `--emit-rows`, which is the
file's rule: 61 → 67 rows, 40 → 46 of 216 names witnessed.

**Decision (b): a guard nobody can reach is not a guard, so it becomes step 11.** `grep` for
`check_falsifier_registry` across the gate script, the Makefile and CI returns the checker itself and
nothing else: D103 wrote it, D113 tightened it, and in between it ran when a person remembered to pass
`--db` — which is the same defect this lane fixed for the truncate probe (step 6), for the comment plane
(step 9) and for the two-ledger comparison (step 10). The gate now runs it against `$GATE_DB` while that
database still exists, with `NEXUS_FALSIFIERS` as the reachability knob so the step can be shown red
without editing the shipped file while ten other steps read it — the shape `LEDGER_SECTIONS_DIR` gives step
10. Its first shipped word on the matter is that a green gate now means every witness row still opens.

**What the measurement corrected.** `check_falsifier_registry.mjs`'s own header asserted that "103 of the
216 names are built at run time by the polymorphic sweeps". The claim is checkable with one rule — a name is
assembled iff its quoted constant is absent from `quality.sql` — and that rule gives 101 today, all 101 carrying
a `: ` prefix, 0 exceptions. The 103 is D98's, measured by that same rule on the same 216-name plane (D98
records 111 occurring once, 2 twice, 103 absent), so this unit's first correction was itself wrong: a note here
blamed the gap on the 214 plane, and 214 was never D98's denominator. Reproducing it as far as the tree allows:
D98's own committed file text against today's live names gives 102 assembled (112 · 2 · 102, against the
recorded 111 · 2 · 103) and the working copy gives 101, so one name is D107's rename of the `documents` row and
the last one cannot be reconstructed at all — D98's live name set is not in the repository, and because the
sweeps build names from the catalogue, an equal total is not the same total. That is the whole reason the file
now states the rule and leaves the count out.

The other number in play was a mirage of the same kind. #73 carries "74 literal names unwitnessed", which is
D117's queue read off a 214-name dump: 109 literal-named, 35 witnessed, 74 unwitnessed. This unit's 74 is
115 literal minus 41 witnessed on a 216 plane. Two numerators, two subtrahends, one coincident difference — and
putting the candidate rules on the same 216 names at the same moment removes the coincidence: constant-presence
splits them **115 / 101** (41 of the literal ones witnessed → 74 unwitnessed), the sweep-prefix literals mined
from the file **116 / 100** (75), and "any name beginning `<word>: `" **101 / 115** (66). 74 is a true reading
of exactly one rule, so calling it a reproduction claimed arithmetic, not the gate. The disagreements carry
their own mechanism: the prefix rule files `density: >= 300 merchants within 3km of Sha Tin` as literal, but
quality.sql:524 builds it as `'density: >= ' || :MIN_NEAR_SHA_TIN || ' merchants within 3km of Sha Tin'`, so it
*is* assembled and only constant-presence sees that; the other 14 disagreements run the other way — whole
constants at quality.sql:170, :888 and :939 that merely begin with a colon-prefixed word (`volume: chunks > 0`,
`slots: 21-day horizon…`, `chunks: token size…`). Constant-presence is the rule the checker states because it is
the only one that asks how a name was produced. Rule to keep: report the split *and* the rule that produced it,
and never let equal differences stand in for equal measurements.

**Consequences, and the limits of them.** Two of the six arms land on `facts`, the one table with no CHECKs
that #71 keeps reporting, so `price facts respect the 6h TTL` and `some facts are deliberately stale` went
from never-seen-red to seen-red twice; that strengthens #71's case rather than settling it, because the
option now has a measured cost (without the CHECK those two rows are the only thing between a wrong TTL and
a served page). Collateral split by a mechanism for the first time: the four arms touching
`merchants`/`facts` carried spread rows and the two touching `reviews`/`permission_grants` carried none, and
`pg_trigger` says why — 15 tables carry `set_updated_at` and those two are not among them — so the spread
census is now predictable from the trigger list instead of only explicable afterwards. The 91 `fk: ` names
are the bulk of what is left, and they are cheap-but-not-free: D105 reddened FK guards through the schema's
own constraints, which is a different mechanism from a `qc` row going red, so witnessing those names needs a
plant that survives the constraint. And one honesty note about this decision's own artifact: the checker
computes its coverage percentage from whatever registry file it is handed, so the planted scratch run
reported "1 of 216" while naming both defects — correct as a refusal, misleading if a log line is quoted
without the `--registry` that produced it.

## D119 The volume plane: six assertions no fabricated value can reach, because they read a snapshot of `count(*)` — 2026-09-27

D118 aimed at values; this unit aimed at sizes. All six `volume: ` assertions read `counts`, the temp table
quality.sql fills with `count(*)` at its own top (quality.sql:97) and asks again at quality.sql:160-174, so no
fabricated URL, marker, stamp or name can move one — the only deception available on that plane is the size of a
table. A DELETE is also a different promise than an UPDATE: an UPDATE has to survive the schema's CHECKs, while
a DELETE has to survive the referential closure, and those are read out of different catalogue columns.

**Decision (a): legality measured one table over, before anything was aimed.** `pg_constraint` grouped by
`confrelid` gives the inbound keys and their `confdeltype`: every referencer of `merchants` is CASCADE except
four NO ACTION keys (carts, handoffs, orders, reservations), and every referencer of `offerings` is CASCADE
except cart_items, order_items, reservations and reviews. Those NO ACTION tables are empty in the seed —
measured 0/0/0/0 for carts/cart_items/reservations/handoffs, orders and reservations being required-empty by
§109 — so no delete can be refused for a reason the gate would then be blamed for. `reviews` and `chunks` have
no inbound FK at all. With the closure settled, each arm is aimed so that only its own volume row moves: 21
merchants taken fewest-reviews-first from a pool lying outside a bbox of lat < 22.30 or lng > 114.25; 535
offerings referenced by no review, no fact and no document; 1,001 reviews deleted in the table's own 31/69
language ratio so the mix row reads 69.10% → 69.11%; documents protected to one per merchant.

**Decision (b): the margin that had to be broken before the run.** `volume: documents >= merchants` is 1,040
against 520 — a margin of exactly the merchant count — so the protected sweep lands on 520 = 520, which is
legal, green and worth nothing. Breaking the tie means one merchant losing its last document, so the arm is
two statements and the second one is the finding. A probe in one rolled-back transaction (BEGIN/plant/SELECT/
ROLLBACK against the kept loaded seed) caught that in seconds; without it the same lesson costs a whole-gate
session and a red-looking drive.

**Decision (c): what the drive filed.** Baseline 216 assertions red 0. The six volume arms reddened their own
row with collateral 5, 0, 7, 1, 3, 10; the control re-ran arm 0 with the triggers off and returned target RED,
collateral 0, spread row gone; the closing baseline is identical to the opening one; 32 arms plus the control
across 35 whole-gate sessions (printed 67; D120), every one rolled back; `RESULT: PASS`. The rows entered `data/seed/falsifiers.tsv`
only from that run's own `--emit-rows`: **67 → 73 rows, 46 → 52 of 216 names witnessed (24.1%)**. Collateral on
this plane is structural rather than incidental — a delete removes rows from other assertions' denominators, so
the merchants arm necessarily reddens the favourites and moderation orphans its CASCADE reached — and the two
arms that came back with low or zero collateral are the two whose deletes touch nothing that anything counts.

**Found (a): the plane is data-dependent — the facts arm filed 213 assertions, not 216.** Measured after the
run in one rolled-back transaction: the three names that leave are `orphan: facts.location`,
`orphan: facts.merchant` and `orphan: facts.offering`, because quality.sql:381 builds them as
`'orphan: facts.' || t … GROUP BY subject_type`, so a subject type with no rows files no row at all. D118's
lesson was that an equal total is not the same set; this is the same lesson on a second axis — the total itself
moves with the data, so a coverage denominator is a reading of the plane as much as of the file.

**Found (b): the harness polices redness, not existence, so (a) passed it by.** Reading the shipped arithmetic
in the per-arm block (data/seed/falsifier_plants.py:1270-1292): collateral is `reds not in base_reds`, and `base_reds` is the set of
*red* rows on unmutated data. A name that stops being filed is therefore invisible to every test the drive
makes — the 213 was printed in the `rows` column and caught by a person reading it, not by the verdict. A drive
whose arm deletes the table a sweep groups over can report PASS while three assertions leave the plane, and
nothing in the record says so. Queue: compare each session's filed name SET against the baseline name set, the
way the red set is already compared.

**Found (c): a distance number that was invented twice, then measured.** The plants commit message says the 62
eligible merchants are "at least 7 km from Sha Tin", and this unit's own draft said 6.4 km. Neither was a
measurement: 6.42 km is the geometric bound at the bbox corner (114.25 − 114.1876° at cos 22.38°), 7 was that
rounded up, and the data's nearest eligible merchant is **10.51 km** from the gate's own anchor, with the 21
deleted spanning 10.51–18.23 km — measured with `pg_temp.haversine_m` exactly as quality.sql:36-42 defines it
against (22.3831, 114.1876). The claim that matters (the density row's 3 km radius cannot notice) holds with
3.5× the clearance either figure claimed, so the plant was never at risk — but the number written down was
arithmetic on a box, not on the rows inside it. Rule: when a plant's safety rests on a geometric margin, run
the gate's distance function over the candidate pool; a bbox corner bounds the box, not the data.

**Found (d): eleven assertions were shown red by this drive and the record does not say so.** Crossing the
drive's collateral lines against the registry: 22 distinct names reddened as collateral, 11 of them already
witnessed by their own arm, **11 with no row** — among them `orphan: favorites.offering`, which went red
because the merchants delete cascade-killed the offering its unenforced reference pointed at, which is the
precise deception that assertion was written to watch. By D103's own standard — a witness records an assertion
*shown able to fail* — those are witnesses, and `--emit-rows` drops them because it files only the matched
target (falsifier_plants.py:293-294). D120's candidate: let a drive offer its collateral names too, with the
arm column naming the arm that happened to redden them, so the record says what the run showed.

**Consequences, and what they cost.** One more mechanism note on `facts`, the table #71 keeps reporting: it has
exactly one outbound FK (`facts.merchant_id → merchants` ON DELETE CASCADE) and 0 CHECKs, which is why the
empty-table plant reached the gate alive — nothing references `facts`, so no closure had to be measured for that
arm at all. Conversely `favorites` carries exactly one FK (`user_id → users`), so the four `orphan: favorites.*`
names in the queue have no schema resistance either, and their legality is now measured rather than assumed —
that is the next batch, and it is one UPDATE per name. The queue recomputed off the same 216-name dump:
**164 unwitnessed = 68 literal + 96 assembled**, i.e. all six new witnesses came out of the literal bucket and
the assembled half did not move — which is what a volume batch should do, since every `volume: ` constant is
written out in quality.sql. Remaining families: fk 91, no-prefix 66, orphan 4, and chunks/density/slots 1 each.

## D120 An assertion can stop existing instead of going red, a collateral red turns out to be a witness, and the harness's own session count was arithmetic — 2026-09-27

**Why this is a tool unit.** D119 closed with three findings, two of them about the plant harness rather than
the seed: an arm that made assertions *stop existing* had passed the drive unnoticed, and the record of what
had been shown able to fail dropped every collateral red. Both are verdicts now. The third — a session count
that came from arithmetic — reached further back into the ledgers than the unit that found it. A fourth found
this unit's own printout wrong, and it is here because the check that caught it is the same one as (a) and (b):
read the tool's output back against the artifact it writes.

**Decision (a): existence is judged, not assumed.** An arm may declare the names it unfiles (an optional
fourth tuple element); an undeclared disappearance fails the drive. The mechanism is one more aggregated row
per session: the baseline name list is passed back into each arm's transaction and the session reports which
of those names `qc` no longer holds. Shown red before green, on the facts arm exactly as D119 left it —
without the declaration `RESULT: FAIL` naming `orphan: facts.location`, `orphan: facts.merchant` and
`orphan: facts.offering`, exit 1; with it the same three print as `unfiled, declared`, the closing baseline
reads identical, exit 0. The transport states its own precondition instead of trusting it: names ride one row
separated by chr(31), so the baseline session counts names carrying a tab, newline or that separator (measured
today: 0 of 216) and stops the run on a non-zero answer rather than mis-splitting a name.

**Decision (b): a collateral red is a witness, so it can be filed.** D103's standard is that the registry
records assertions *shown able to fail*, and an assertion the gate reddened because a plant also moved
something it watches has been shown. `--emit-rows` files those names too, deduplicated by check, with the arm
column naming the arm that ran — which is the honest sentence, because the arm does not claim it was aimed
there. Shown first on one merchants-delete session against a scratch copy of the registry: 5 rows appended, 0
of them the arm's own target (already filed), the validator over that file answering `RESULT: PASS` at 54 of
216, and the same session run again appending 0.

**Decision (c): the session count was a formula, and the correction is backwards.** The closing line printed
`2 * len(ARMS) + 3` whole-gate sessions while the loop calls the gate once per arm — the true figure is
`arms + 3` (baseline, one per arm, control, closing). Four drives of this lane quoted the inflated number, and
every ledger line that repeated it inherited the error: 13 arms said 29 and ran 16, 20 said 43 and ran 23, 26
said 55 and ran 29, 32 said 67 and ran 35. Seven lines across the two ledgers are corrected in place here, the
oldest from D109. Nothing else in those entries depended on the count, which is why it survived eleven units:
a number that only ever appears in prose has no reader to disagree with it.

**Decision (d): the row-split the emission prints was a name test dressed as provenance.** (b) shipped with a
closing line — `registry rows appended: 22 (4 from the arm's own target, 18 from its collateral)` — and reading
the file it wrote says 0 of those 22 rows came from a target. Every one came from `collateral_witnessed`; the
four "targets" were collateral rows that happen to name an assertion some *other* arm was aimed at, because the
line tested `name in {every arm's marker}` instead of which list the row was emitted from. Same shape as (a):
a verdict computed from the wrong set, printed in a run that exited 0, in a sentence nothing downstream parses.
Provenance now travels with the pair (`own` / `collateral`) rather than being re-derived from names, and the
line states both currencies, because rows and assertions are not the same count: a row keys on
(check, arm) so a second arm can witness an already-witnessed name, while coverage counts distinct names.
Shown on one arm with `--only` against a scratch copy of the HEAD registry — 5 rows appended, `0 emitted from
an arm's own RED row, 5 from collateral · 2 of them name an assertion that carried no witness before`. The
discriminating evidence is the file itself, read back: of the 22 rows that drive appended, **0** carry a name
containing their own arm's marker, so not one came from the target list, and the four the old line named as
targets are four collateral rows whose assertion another arm happens to be aimed at.

**The drive that certified all four.** The same 32 arms plus the trigger control, re-run against the kept
loaded seed with `--emit-rows` pointing at the shipped registry: baseline 216 assertions red 0; every arm's own
row RED; the facts arm still filing 213 and now declaring the three names it unfiles, so the run that would
have failed a commit ago passes with the disappearance on the record instead of in a column; control target
RED, collateral 0, unfiled 0, spread row gone; closing baseline identical; **35 whole-gate sessions counted**;
`RESULT: PASS`; **22 rows appended**, all of them from collateral (decision (d) — the line that ran printed
"4 from the arm's own target", which the file contradicts).
`data/seed/falsifiers.tsv` 73 → **95 rows**, coverage **52 → 63 of 216 (29.2%)**: eleven assertions gained a
witness from a drive that planted nothing new — 22 rows bought 11 names, because a row keys on (check, arm) and
coverage counts names — which is the whole argument for the emission rule.

**What the harvest did to the queue.** Recomputed off the same 216-name dump: 164 unwitnessed → **153 = 58
literal + 95 assembled** — the first time the assembled bucket moved (96 → 95), because collateral does not
care how a name was produced. Families left: `fk ` 91, no-prefix 56, `orphan ` 3, chunks/density/slots 1 each.
Three of the four `orphan: favorites.*` names §128 named as the next batch are already witnessed — witnessed by
accident, by a delete aimed at a merchant count. That is what filing what the gate showed buys, and what
filing only what was aimed for loses; the cost is that a row's arm column can describe a plant that happens to
have moved the assertion rather than one designed to defeat it, and the reader has to keep that distinction.

**Limits, stated rather than implied.** The guard reads one direction: it reports baseline names a session
stopped filing, and says nothing about a name that appears only under a plant. D119 measured the born-set on
the one arm that moved the plane and found 0, so no mechanism is known — if one turns up, the reversed
predicate is the same query, not a new tool. And coverage is counted by *name*, so an arm filing a name
another arm already filed adds a second witness without moving the percentage: right for a record of
demonstrations, wrong as a budget. Step 11 still computes its percentage from whatever `--registry` it is
handed (§127's residue), so the scratch runs quoted above are refusals to be read with their file, not totals.

## D121 Three arms move a PAIR instead of a value, the two cheap ones reddened nothing else, and that turned out to be two probes disagreeing — 2026-09-27

Why this is a data unit. §129's next(b) named three assertions and measured their legality before aiming: over
`pg_constraint`, `favorites` carries exactly one foreign key (`user_id` → users CASCADE) and `facts` exactly one
(`merchant_id` → merchants CASCADE), and `subject_id` is in neither; neither column carries a CHECK. So each of
the three deceptions is one UPDATE. They are the first arms in this lane whose falsehood is the **pairing**
rather than a value, a count or a stamp: the `subject_type` string keeps its meaning and the `subject_id` names
a row that really exists, in another table's role.

**Decision (a): the two favourite arms lie by label.** `data/seed/falsifier_plants.py:238-243` points the one
`collection` favourite at the `kind='guide'` row and the one `guide` favourite at a `kind='collection'` row.
`collections` is 4 rows — guide 1, collection 2, itinerary 1 — all four `visibility='public'` with
`published_at` set and an `author_id`; `favorites` is 18 rows (merchant 12, offering 4, collection 1, guide 1).
quality.sql:306-307 pins each label to the row's own kind exactly the way `assertSubjectInTenant` pins it, so a
mislabelled favourite is precisely what that probe was written to catch, and it is a different deception from
pointing at nothing: the join resolves, the row is publishable, only the type lies.

**Decision (b): the facts arm lies by table.** One merchant fact is re-keyed onto an offering's id
(`falsifier_plants.py:236-239`), chosen at `attribute='opening_hours'` so the price-TTL and rating witnesses
stay uncontested. `facts_one_row_per_claim_uidx` is on `(subject_type, subject_id, attribute)` and does not
object, because the triple is still unique; nothing references the table.

**Decision (c): the batch is cheap because `--only` exists.** Three arms plus the two baseline sessions are
**5 whole-gate sessions**; the 35-arm harvest is 38. A three-arm batch run on its own is a test, and the full
drive afterwards is a harvest rather than a re-test — the order matters for the cost, and it is the reason this
unit's numbers came from both.

**The finding: zero collateral on the two favourite arms is a disagreement, not cleanliness.** The drive printed
`collateral 0` for both, which reads like a perfectly aimed plant. The renderability companion
(`favourites point at a renderable row`, quality.sql:1073-1089) joins `collections` on the id with **no `kind`
condition** (quality.sql:1077), and its WHERE (quality.sql:1078-1084) branches only on `merchant`, `offering`
and `collection` — there is no `guide` clause at all. So a mislabelled collection favourite still lands on a
public, published, authored row and stays green, and a guide favourite is invisible to the probe in every
direction. Measured on the kept loaded seed, four plants, each rolled back, the gate body sliced from the shipped
file rather than re-derived:

| plant | `orphan: favorites.*` | `favourites point at a renderable row` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| nothing planted (control) | all four true | true |
| collection favourite → the guide row | collection **false** | true |
| guide favourite → a collection row | guide **false** | true |
| collection favourite → a uuid nothing holds | collection **false** | **false** |
| guide favourite → a uuid nothing holds | guide **false** | true |

The fourth row reproduces D100's claim — "one broken edge answers both, and both answered" — for the
`collection` type. The fifth is the correction: the companion answers for three of the four types the door
accepts, because it has no `guide` branch, and the first two rows show the other half of the boundary — it
answers for a missing target, not for a mislabelled one. D100 wrote the pairing as a property of the seam, and
it is a property of that probe's arm list, which is the same class of statement D119 had to make about the
volume plane: a companion is load-bearing only where its own WHERE reaches.

**The fix shape, reported and not made.** Give the CTE a `guide` branch carrying the same publishability
predicates, and `AND c.kind = 'collection'` on the collection branch. Both would be green on today's seed — the
two kind-pinned orphan arms are green unmutated, which is D67's generator fix (`kind=kind` threaded through)
still holding. So this is a falsifiability gap, not a live lie, and it is not edited here: `data/seed/quality.sql`
is another lane's working copy right now (` M` in `git status`). D67 reported that the favourites probe "has no
`guide` arm for a type the door does accept"; that half is now closed on the sweep side — the probe assembles
its names from the data (quality.sql:312) and `orphan: favorites.guide` exists and reddens — while the open half
has moved to the companion.

**The other six rows, and what the arm column actually means.** 9 rows were appended: 3 carry a D121 arm label,
6 carry an older arm's. Read back off the file, that is exactly what the `(check, arm)` key D120 chose predicts:
the `facts.merchant` arm reddened two further assertions, and neither row names it, because the phone arm and
the fact-stamp arm reddened those same names earlier in the same drive and had not been filed at HEAD. The
column means "an arm that has been shown to move this name", not "the arm this unit added" — which is what D120
said a row is for, and worth stating again because a reader counting witnesses per unit would otherwise count
these six against D121's cost.

**Numbers.** `data/seed/falsifiers.tsv` 95 → **104 rows**, names covered 63 → **66 of 216 (30.6%)**, witness
kinds 65 commit + 39 file, step 11 RESULT PASS on the final bytes. Unwitnessed 153 → **150 = 58 literal + 92
assembled**. By family: `fk ` 91, no-prefix 56, chunks/density/slots 1 each, and **`orphan ` 3 → 0** — the
family D65 opened is now fully witnessed. Three arms bought three names; six rows bought none, so this is the
lowest marginal-witness rate the lane has run per row (1 name per 3 rows) and the highest per arm (1 name per
arm, D120's 22-for-11 included nothing aimed).

**Limits, stated rather than implied.** The guide-blindness result is measured against this working copy's 216
assertions; if the other lane's `quality.sql` edit adds a branch to that CTE the probe has to be re-run before
the table above is quoted again. The four plants above are diagnostic sessions, not registry rows — nothing was
filed from them, and the two that reddened no new name could not be.

**next.** The `fk ` family is 91 of the remaining 150 and none of them is plantable by a legal write, because

(`ERROR: insert or update on table "reviews" violates foreign key constraint "reviews_merchant_id_fkey"`) and
applied under replica role (`UPDATE 1`, the new id returned). So every one of the 91 is reachable, and the

whose whole job is to watch a write the database refuses falsified by a database the database cannot produce —
or only by one a restore, a legacy import or a dump-from-another-instance could put in the loader's chair?

## D122 The `fk: ` family cannot be falsified by a legal write, so the plant says on its face that the checks are off — and the route a deployment can take falsifies a different assertion — 2026-09-27

§130 put the question before the batch. This unit answers it with three measurements, and the answer is *yes,
conditionally* — followed by a finding that splits the family in two.

**Decision (a): a witness may be produced with the checks disabled, provided the arm's own label says so.** Nine
arms went into `data/seed/falsifier_plants.py` (:269-317), each `SET LOCAL session_replication_role = replica;`
followed by one UPDATE of one foreign-key column to a `gen_random_uuid()`. Three conditions were measured rather
than argued, because "the tool disabled the thing the assertion watches" is exactly the sentence that needs
evidence attached to it:

| measurement | result | what it buys |
| --- | --- | --- |
| the SET alone, nothing moved | 216 rows, 0 red | the mechanism reddens nothing on its own — the dangling id does |
| `rating = 9.9` and `body = NULL` under the same SET | both refused (`reviews_rating_check`, not-null violation) | the role silences foreign keys and triggers, **not** CHECKs or NOT NULLs, so an `fk: ` arm cannot smuggle a value-plane lie past a value-plane assertion |
| each of the nine arms | 216 rows, exactly 1 red, 0 collateral, 0 names born, 0 names vanished | the aim is as exact as the polymorphic batch's |

The label carries `(replica role)` because the label is what lands in the registry's arm column: a reader of
`data/seed/falsifiers.tsv` must not be able to mistake the row for a demonstration that some door can produce an
orphan. It cannot, and that is measured too — as `nexus_app`, the role the services connect with, the same `SET`
is refused: `permission denied to set parameter "session_replication_role"`. The plant's power is precisely the
application's missing power, which is what makes these rows backstops on the data plane rather than tests of a
write path.

**Decision (b): the route a deployment CAN take is filed as a witness for a different name.** A migration that
stops enforcing an edge is reachable, so a tenth arm does that: `ALTER TABLE user_preferences DROP CONSTRAINT
user_preferences_user_id_fkey`, then the same orphaning UPDATE, then ROLLBACK (the DDL is transactional — the
constraint counts 1 again afterwards, measured). It does **not** falsify `fk: user_preferences.user_id ->
users.id`. That session files **215** assertions: the sweep builds its names from `pg_constraint`, so when the
constraint goes, the name goes — D120's disappearance, reached deliberately this time — and the row that turns
red instead is D66's `every reference the seed writes is probed or explained`, which reads the same catalogue and
notices that an edge left the probed set. The arm therefore declares the vanished name rather than filing it,
and files the census row, which is what the drop actually demonstrates.

So the ninety-one names were two claims in one prefix, and the split is the useful part: *"does every value in
this column resolve?"* is a question about data, and only a checks-off session can produce a data state the
schema forbids; *"is this edge still enforced?"* is a question about the schema, and a migration can answer it —
but then the sweep row is not the thing watching, the census row is.

**Decision (c): an assertion that is green for want of data is recorded as such, in the label.**
`moderation_cases.assigned_to` has 544 rows and **0** carry an assignee, so the sweep row has never resolved a
single value: the first attempt — move an existing assignee to a ghost — moved nothing and the arm stayed green
for the right reason. The filed plant files the column first (`SET assigned_to = gen_random_uuid()` on a row
that had none) and its label says `(0 of 544 carry one)`. That is D79's "probe arms the seed never files are
silence, not green" arriving on the enforcement plane, and it is the same shape as 50 of the remaining 82 names,
whose child tables have no rows at all.

**Numbers.** Aimed subset (`--only 'fk: '`) 10 arms, 12 whole-gate sessions, PASS; the full drive 45 arms plus the
control, 48 sessions, PASS. `data/seed/falsifiers.tsv` 104 → **116 rows**, **12 appended** (10 from an arm's own
RED row, 2 from collateral) · **10 of them a name that carried no witness before** — the first batch this lane has
run where every appended target row is a novel name, because the family had none. Coverage 66 → **76 of 216
(35.2%)**, witness kinds 77 commit + 39 file, step 11 PASS. Unwitnessed 150 → **140 = 57 literal + 83 assembled**;
the `fk ` family 91 → **82 left, and the remainder splits 50 on a child table the seed leaves empty and 32 on a
populated one**.

**Limits, stated rather than implied.** These ten rows demonstrate detection, not reachability, and no wording in
the registry should be read as claiming otherwise — the arm column is the only place that distinction survives,
which is why the labels are as long as they are. The `SET` is available only to a superuser session in the
container, so the witness cannot be reproduced by the deployment role; that is the point of the mechanism and the
reason the family stays a backstop. And the cheap part is nearly over: the 32 populated-child names are one-line
arms of this exact shape, while the 50 empty-child names need an INSERT each — NOT NULL and CHECK survive the
role (measured above), so each needs a complete legal row built from a table that has no rows to copy.

**next.** (a) The 32 remaining populated-child names in batches of about ten, each one UPDATE behind the same SET.
(b) Then the question the empty tables raise before their arms are written: is an `fk: ` row over a table the seed
never populates worth witnessing with a synthetic INSERT, or is the honest record D79's — silence, not green — and
the lane should say so once for 50 names instead of fifty times. (c) #71, fifth time standing on it. (d) Carried
from §130: the renderability companion's missing `guide` branch, reported and not edited.

## D123 The falsification queue is per COLUMN, not per child table — and four of the ten plants found a companion that reads the same column — 2026-09-27

§131's next(a) was a batch plan read off a table-level split: "the 32 populated-child names in batches of about
ten, each one UPDATE behind the same SET". This unit takes ten of them, and the measurement done before aiming
shows the split was the wrong plane to plan from.

**Decision (a): aim from the column, not the child table.** All 32 candidate columns were read off the kept
database first — rows total, rows carrying a value, the constraints naming the column, any CHECK bounding it (a
rolled-back DO block, scratch `d123_aim.sql`). Two of the 32 cannot be falsified by an UPDATE at all:
`categories.tenant_id` has 77 rows and **0** carry a value, and `documents.offering_id` has 1040 rows and **0**
carry one. The sweep counts `WHERE c.col IS NOT NULL AND p.col IS NULL`, so on those columns it has never
resolved anything — an UPDATE has nothing to move, and the honest arm is D122's shape (file the value, then
dangle it). They stayed out of this batch. Three more are sparse rather than empty: `resource_pools.offering_id`
7 of 452, `reviews.user_id` 245 of 11000, `reviews.offering_id` 2055 of 11000 — an UPDATE reaches those, but the
row resolves a fraction of the column while its detail prints only the orphan count, so a 98%-NULL column and a
fully-populated one print identically. That is D79's "silence, not green" arriving on the enforcement plane with
a new twist: there the probe emitted *no check*, here it emits a check whose coverage is invisible from its own
answer. Reported, not edited — `data/seed/quality.sql` is another lane's working copy, and the fix would be to
print `n resolved of m non-null` in the detail, not to weaken the verdict.

What the census did buy is the handle: no column in the batch is a primary key and none is bounded by a CHECK, so
`WHERE id = (SELECT id FROM t ORDER BY id LIMIT 1)` is legal for all ten (falsifier_plants.py:330-379), and the
seven columns that sit inside some composite UNIQUE cannot collide with it, because the new value is a random
uuid. This also retires §129's failed probe: `offering_relations` has no `id` column at all, and both of its
names are still in the queue, keyed on the pair.

**Decision (b): four of the ten arms are not single-row witnesses, and the collateral they found is a witness
for real.** `availability_slots.merchant_id`, `chunks.document_id`, `documents.merchant_id` and
`locations.merchant_id` each reddened exactly one companion besides their own name — `slots: every slot has a
pool in the same merchant`, `chunks: ordinal contiguous per document`, `merchant has a menu document (RAG feed)`,
`merchant has a primary location` — while the other six arms, including all three `.tenant_id` ones, reddened
nothing else. The pattern is that the companion reaches the child's *merchant* (or its *document*) through the
very column being danglinged, so the same-scope predicate stops holding the moment the id becomes a ghost; the
tenant-scoped arms find nothing because no companion in the file joins on `tenant_id` for those tables. One of
the four, `slots: every slot has a pool in the same merchant`, had never carried a witness before this drive and
now has one, filed from collateral — the third consecutive batch where the by-product is the more interesting
row (D121's phone arm, D122's stamp arms, this one).

**Decision (c): the rows were filed by the second, identical drive, because the first one's witness was the
wrong commit.** The first drive PASSed with the same 55 arms and the same 16 rows, but it was handed `--witness
c6b1018` — the ledgers' commit, which does not contain the arms. A witness has to be an artifact that carries
the thing it testifies to, so the registry was restored from HEAD, the harness was committed on its own as
`499bfa4`, and the drive was re-run against that sha. The two transcripts then diff to **zero** apart from the
witness column: 58 whole-gate sessions each on one kept database, same per-arm verdicts, same closing baseline.
That is also the first chance this lane has had to check its own rollback discipline across two full drives —
116 write sessions in one day, and the second drive sees the same 216 assertions and 0 baseline reds as the
first.

**Numbers.** Arms 45 → 55. `data/seed/falsifiers.tsv` 116 → **132 rows**, 16 appended (10 from an arm's own RED
row, 6 from collateral) over 16 distinct names, **11 of them a name that carried no witness before**. Coverage 76
→ **87 of 216 (40.3%)**; witness kinds 93 commit + 39 file; step 11 PASS. Unwitnessed 140 → **129 = 56
literal + 73 assembled**; the `fk ` family 82 → **72 = 50 on an empty child table + 22 on a populated one**, and
of those 22 the two zero-value columns above are not reachable by an UPDATE, so **20** names are left on the
cheap route.

**Limits.** D122's still stand: these rows demonstrate detection, not reachability, and the state exists only in
a session the `nexus_app` role is refused. New limit from this batch: a companion witnessed from collateral was
witnessed under a checks-off state, so it testifies that the companion notices a broken merchant link — it says
nothing about whether a *legal* write can produce a same-merchant mismatch, which is the risk that companion was
written against. Reading those four rows as door tests would over-claim exactly as D122 warned.

**next.** (a) The 20 genuinely UPDATE-reachable names in two batches, and the two zero-value columns folded into
a value-filing arm each. (b) The decision the 50 empty-child names raise, plus a second question the sparse
columns raise: whether a `fk: ` row should print how many values it resolved, which is a `quality.sql` change and
therefore another lane's file. (c) #71, sixth time standing on it. (d) Carried from §130: the renderability
companion's missing `guide` branch, reported and not edited.

## D124 The cheap half of the `fk: ` family is closed, so a row selector now has to know whether the column carries a value on *that* row — 2026-09-27

D123's next(a) was "the 20 genuinely UPDATE-reachable names in two batches, and the two zero-value columns folded
into a value-filing arm each". This unit does all 22 in one batch, because the two things that made ten the right
size last time — the cost of aiming and the cost of driving — both fell: the census is a read-only query set run
in one shell step, and a drive of three whole-gate sessions timed at **11 s** here, so 80 of them are minutes, not
a milestone.

**Decision (a): close the half, then say what the remaining half actually is.** After these 22 arms the family
reads 91 filed names, **41 witnessed, 50 left, and 0 of the 50 sit on a populated child table** — every one of
them is on a table the seed leaves empty (27 tables, exactly 0 rows each). So the queue is no longer "keep aiming
the same plant at the next column": what is left needs an INSERT, which is a different claim about a different
reachability, and it goes to D125 as a decision rather than staying here as a remainder.

**Decision (b): the row selector inherits D123's per-column lesson, and the arms are written to match.** Three of
the 20 dense columns are sparse — `resource_pools.offering_id` 7 of 452, `reviews.offering_id` 2055 of 11000,
`reviews.user_id` 245 of 11000 — so `ORDER BY id LIMIT 1` is overwhelmingly likely to pick a row where the column
is NULL. An UPDATE there is not "an edge is cut"; it is "a value was invented, then an edge was cut", two claims
in one arm, and the second one is exactly what the two zero-value arms are for. Therefore all 20 cut-arms select
with `<col> IS NOT NULL` and the 2 file-arms select with `<col> IS NULL`, and each label prints the fraction
(`falsifier_plants.py:399-510`). Two of the 22 also needed a handle that is not `id`: `merchant_categories` is
keyed `(merchant_id, category_id)` and `offering_relations` `(from_offering, to_offering, relation)`, and in
three cases the danglinged column is itself a key member, which is only safe because the new value is a random
uuid. The 2 value-filing arms reddened nothing else, which is the cleanest witness this family can produce: one
write, one assertion noticing.

**Decision (c): the merchant-tenant arm reddened two assertions whose names never mention merchants.** 13 of the
22 arms are clean; 9 reddened 22 companion lines over 14 distinct names. The interesting three come from
`merchants.tenant_id`: `everything hangs off the single demo tenant`, plus `a view answer names the kind the
census derives` and `a view kind is exercised or exempted` — the last two had **never** carried a witness before.
Read out of the file (quality.sql:628 and :3342, :3377) the mechanism is not a join: the tenant row compares
`tenant_id <> '0000…0001'`, so it sees the new value directly, and the view census *derives* each served column's
kind by counting its values, so a write that makes one merchant's tenant unresolvable flips a column from `const`
to something else and the hand-written answer no longer matches the derived kind. Worth stating plainly as a limit
(below): a companion caught by a value predicate is a weaker witness than one caught by the join the companion was
written for.

**Numbers.** Arms 55 → **77**. Two drives, both read here: a targeted pre-flight over the 40 checks-off arms
(42 whole-gate sessions, PASS, control skipped because `--only` excluded arm 0) run first so that a bad new arm
fails in three minutes instead of five, then the full drive — 77 arms + 1 control, **80 sessions**, PASS, control
target red with its spread collateral gone, closing baseline 216 assertions and 0 reds, identical to opening.
`data/seed/quality.sql` md5 `4d3a707e…` identical before and after, so the whole drive read the file this lane
read. Registry 132 → **170 rows**: 38 appended (22 from an arm's own RED row, 16 from collateral) over 38 distinct
names — the drive dedups by name, so a companion three arms reddened in one run is filed once — of which **29**
carried no witness before. 14 of those 16 collateral rows come from this batch's arms; the other 2 name an
assertion reddened by an arm from an earlier batch that the full drive re-ran, whose `(check, arm)` pair no targeted
run had ever emitted — so a full drive harvests second witnesses a targeted one structurally cannot see. Coverage 87 → **116 of 216 = 53.7%**, past half for the first time; witness kinds 131
commit + 39 file; step 11 PASS. Unwitnessed 129 → **100 = 49 literal + 51 assembled**. `fk` family 72 → **50**,
all on an empty child; those 27 tables carry 57 outgoing FKs in total, of which 7 are not even swept because their
parent is another empty table.

**Limits.** D122's and D123's stand: these rows demonstrate detection under a state the `nexus_app` role is
refused, and a companion witnessed from collateral says nothing about whether a legal write could produce what it
catches. New to this batch: **41 of 91, and 41 of 41 by one mechanism.** No other family in the registry is that
concentrated — a Postgres upgrade that stopped `session_replication_role` from silencing FKs, or a managed instance
that refuses the GUC entirely, would invalidate all 41 rows at once. And the two filing arms testify on columns
the demo never writes: `categories.tenant_id` and `documents.offering_id` have no tenant-scoped or offering-scoped
data to be wrong about, so what they prove is that the sweep would notice the first value if it ever arrived.

**next.** (a) D125, the empty-child decision, informed by one measurement made here rather than argued: an INSERT
into any closure table outside the anchor also reddens `no traffic outside the seeded tables`, whose own detail

## D125 The last 48 `fk: ` names have to be WRITTEN before they can be dangled, and writing one reddens the assertion that calls the result a non-artifact — 2026-09-27

D124 closed the 41 `fk: ` names whose child table carries rows and left 50 whose child table the seed
leaves empty, over 27 tables. On those the sweep has never resolved anything: it counts
`WHERE c.col IS NOT NULL AND p.col IS NULL` (quality.sql:181-203), and with 0 rows both sides are
empty, so its `0 orphan row(s)` is a statement about nothing. D124's next(a) named the choice — write
a row, or record the 50 as unreachable and spend the batches on the literal names. This unit writes
rows, and files them.

**Decision (a): an empty-child witness is two claims, and only one of them is a falsification.** The
arm is `INSERT …; SET LOCAL session_replication_role = replica; UPDATE … SET col = gen_random_uuid()`.
The INSERT runs while the checks are still ON: every column the schema forces is supplied from a
pg_attribute census rather than from memory (`_MUST`, falsifier_plants.py:614-643), every FK points at
a live id, so the row is legal, not merely tolerated. That half is not a deception at all — it is a
reachability claim, and it is the first one this lane has ever been able to make about 27 tables. The
dangle after it is the D123 mechanism unchanged. D122's limit said a `fk: ` row demonstrates detection
and not reachability; here one arm carries both, and the registry keeps only the second claim's name
next to the row.

**Decision (b): the state is one quality.sql forbids on the artifact, and that is filed rather than
worked around.** 47 of the 48 sessions also redden `no traffic outside the seeded tables`
(quality.sql:263-272), whose own detail then says such a database "is the seed plus traffic, so
quality.sql is reading it as a diagnostic and not as a gate on the artifact". The exception is
instructive: `review_summaries` is one of the 23 anchor tables, so a row there is not traffic outside
the seed — and the dedicated `review_summaries stays empty` reddens instead. Two different assertions
say the same thing about the same state: the demo is not supposed to contain it. So the 48 rows testify
"on a database that carries traffic in this table, the sweep opens it and notices a broken link", not
"a screen can show this". Where the app does write those tables (orders, carts, events, api_keys,
subscriptions…) the assertion is doing real work and the row is worth having; the ledger says which is
which by naming the mechanism in the arm column.

**Decision (c): the derived censuses demand answers as data arrives, so 27 tables contribute nothing to
them at seed.** Across the 48 traffic arms: `every column that cannot vary is answered for why it
cannot` reddened 48 of 48, the two jsonb censuses and the array-element census 7 each,
`every reference the seed writes is probed or explained` and `a seeded polymorphic vocabulary is
bounded or probed` 6 each, `a view kind is exercised or exempted` and `a view answer names the kind the
census derives` 5 each, `a verification badge stays unresolvable…` 10. None of those broke: each
enumerates from the rows, so a table going from 0 to 1 adds columns and pairs to its demand list, and
the list of answers has never been widened for a table the seed does not populate. This is D79's
"silence, not green" again, on the census plane — an assertion that answers every column the demo
carries is silent about 27 tables' worth of schema. Reported, not edited: `data/seed/quality.sql` is
another lane's working copy, and the change would be to answer those columns or to have each census
print how many tables it never opened.

**Decision (d): two names are left out on purpose.** `fk: share_links.created_by -> users.id` and
`fk: share_links.tenant_id -> tenants.id` are 2 of the 50, but share_links exists only on another
lane's uncommitted V7 migration (#75); a witness naming them could not be reopened from a committed
tree. Reachable here: 48, all planted.

**Measurement (e): "tables the seed leaves empty" is not "tables an `fk: ` assertion covers".**
`refunds` needed a payment row to be legal, payments is empty too, and payments needs an order — a
chain three rows deep, which is why `_inserts_for` (falsifier_plants.py:682-691) walks chain deps
transitively instead of one level. `payments` never appeared in the empty-child census at all: the
sweep names only FKs whose parent is in the anchor (quality.sql:192), and payments' single FK points at
orders, which is outside it. The two lists overlap without containing each other, so the census that
plans a batch has to be read as a set difference, not as a description of the schema. The same
discipline caught `review_summaries`: it has no `id` column — its primary key is the very column the
arm dangles, so the row selector keys on it (falsifier_plants.py:541-546). That is D124's lesson about
assuming columns, arriving on the new plane.

**Numbers.** Arms 87 → **125** (ten hand-written at falsifier_plants.py:511-593 to find the shape, 38
generated from it at :594-704). Pre-flight 1: 10 arms, 11 sessions, 9 hit, 1 unread. Pre-flight 2:
38 arms, 39 sessions, 37 hit, 1 unread. Full drive: **125 arms + the control, 128 whole-gate sessions,
RESULT PASS** — every target RED, no arm found an undeclared red, no assertion left the plane
undeclared, closing baseline 216 assertions / 0 red, identical to opening, and
`quality.sql` md5 `4d3a707eff55971b0a2198e2a1b56777` unchanged across all of it. Registry
170 → **236 rows** (66 appended: 48 from an arm's own RED row, 18 from collateral; **55 of them name an
assertion that carried no witness before**). Coverage 116 → **171 of 216 (79.2%)**; witness kinds
197 commit + 39 file; step 11 PASS. Unwitnessed 100 → **45**, of which 2 are share_links, so **43**
are reachable and none of them is a one-UPDATE plant. The `fk: ` family: 91 names, **89 witnessed, 2
left** — both share_links — which closes the family on the committed schema.

**Limits.** (i) Concentration got worse in absolute terms while coverage jumped: of the 171 witnessed
names, **101 have no witness that does not switch the replication role off** (46 whose every witness is
a bare checks-off dangle, 55 whose every witness is a traffic-row arm, which also uses it). No
assertion in that set has been shown to fail by a write the schema itself refuses. (ii) Every row from
this batch is witnessed under a state the gate calls a diagnostic — decision (b). (iii) A companion
reddened by a traffic arm (the 18 rows) was witnessed while the census's scope was changing, not while
its subject was broken, so those rows testify that the census notices new data, which is weaker than
what an `fk: ` row testifies. (iv) 2 of the 45 unwitnessed are the D108 door-vocabulary rows, which are

**next.** (a) The remaining 43 fall into three families and none of them needs a new plant mechanism:

## D126 Eleven arms the schema itself accepts -- the first witnesses this lane has produced without switching a check off — 2026-09-27

D125 closed the `fk: ` family and, reading its own registry backwards, found the shape of the remaining
queue: 101 of the 171 witnessed names had no witness that did not `SET LOCAL
session_replication_role = replica`. That says more about this lane than about the gate -- every one of
D123/D124/D125's plants asks the database to stop enforcing something. D122 had already drawn the line:
a role-switched plant demonstrates detection, not reachability. So this unit asks the opposite question
of the 45 names left: which of them can an assertion lose to a write the database lets through?

**Decision (a): eleven of them can, and the plant is one statement with the checks ON.** A merchant's
whole portfolio moved to another merchant, a one-location merchant's primary location moved away, the
least categorised merchant stripped of every category link, all 544 open review cases closed in one
statement, one queued review published to everyone, every human grant given an expiry date, one fact
made timeless, one opening-hours fact given a 25-hour TTL, an unembedded chunk labelled as embedded,
one slot marked `'live'`, and a feedback event filed under a subject type nobody declared
(falsifier_plants.py:716-776). No ghost uuid appears in any of them -- every id referenced is a row that
exists. Each was legal-tested before aiming: `feedback_events.subject_type` carries no CHECK (D69's
census found the schema bounds only `share_links.subject_type`), `moderation_cases` and
`permission_grants` carry none at all, and `availability_slots` bounds only its times and capacity, so
`source = 'live'` is a value the schema has never heard of and accepts.

**Decision (b): two candidates were dropped or re-aimed while aiming, and both are findings about the
gate.**
  - `price_updated_at present for priced offerings` cannot be reddened by any write, legal or illegal:
    `offerings.price_updated_at` is NOT NULL, and a role switch does not silence NOT NULL either. The
    assertion is implied by the column, so no data state falsifies it. That is D90's "an arm that cannot
    fail" arriving from the other direction -- not a missing plant but a qc row that is documentation
    wearing a check's clothes. Reported; it stays on the 33.
  - the invented subject type slid straight past `no unlisted type rides in the seeded data`, which is
    the row that claims to catch exactly that, because the census only walks the pairs the arm registry
    arms and `feedback_events` is not one of them. The row that DID notice is `a seeded polymorphic
    vocabulary is bounded or probed`, so the arm now testifies for that one (:764-776). Read together
    the two rows say something nobody had measured: an unlisted type on an unarmed pair is invisible to
    the census that names the risk and visible to the one that does not.

**Decision (c): the mass-move shape was forced by measurement, not taste.** No merchant has exactly one
offering (0 of 520) and none has exactly one category link (0 of 520), so a single-row legal write
cannot empty a merchant; those arms move WHOLE portfolios with `WHERE merchant_id = (SELECT …)` -- one
statement, many rows, still a write the schema accepts, and closer to the real failure mode (a
mis-scoped admin query re-parenting everything) than a one-row edit would have been. 520 merchants do
have exactly one primary location, so that arm stayed single-row. The census that decided this is the
same read-only query shape D124 insisted on, run before writing rather than after.

**Numbers.** Arms 125 → **136**; harness `11642b7`. Pre-flight: 11 arms, 13 whole-gate sessions, 10 hit,
1 green (re-aimed above). Full drive: **136 arms + the control, 139 sessions, RESULT PASS** -- every
target RED, nothing undeclared, closing baseline 216 assertions / 0 red identical to opening, and
`quality.sql` md5 `4d3a707eff55971b0a2198e2a1b56777` unchanged. Registry 236 → **267 rows** (31
appended: 11 from an arm's own RED row, 20 from collateral; **12 names carrying no witness before**).
Coverage 171 → **183 of 216 (84.7%)**; witness kinds 228 commit + 39 file; step 11 PASS. Unwitnessed
45 → **33**, of which 2 are share_links' (#75), 1 is the NOT NULL-implied row above, and 1 is the row
the invented type slid past. Companion rows: 12 distinct names, including `merchant has a primary
location`, `category_primary is one of the merchant's own category names`, `every waiting review has
exactly one open case`, `a door vocabulary admits every value the data carries`, both review counters
and the rating-fact restatement, and `no traffic outside the seeded tables` -- once, by the one arm that
writes outside the anchor, which is D125's finding reproduced from the other side.

**Limits.** (i) A legal-write witness is the strongest kind this lane can produce, but it still is not
an application trace: it says the assertion can be lost to a write the database accepts, not that any
endpoint writes that way. (ii) The mechanism census is re-measured here by plant text rather than by arm
label -- 80 of the 183 witnessed names have a witness that touches no `session_replication_role`, and
103 have only ones that do. By that definition D125's 101 is 103, because two arms with prose labels
outside the `checks off` family also issue the SET. (iii) Eleven of the 20 collateral rows were also
produced by a legal write, so their companions inherit claim (i); the `every column that cannot vary…`
row reddened 5 times for the same reason D125 records -- the census's demand list grows with data.
(iv) The 20 collateral rows are witnesses under a state that includes the target's own breakage; they
testify that a companion notices, not that the companion's own risk case is reachable.

**next.** (a) The 33 left fall into three kinds, and only the first has an obvious plant: the

polymorphic-pair census…`, `the arm registry agrees with the probed-pair counts`, `the registry names no

## D127 Eight more legal writes, a census row that reads a key the seed never writes, and the registry's own reader refusing a witness this lane minted — 2026-09-27

D126 opened the legal-write family and left 33 names. This unit aims at the demo-property rows among
them: a merchant's every below-average rating lifted to 4.5, an estimated price's fact re-labelled from
`inferred` to `merchant`, a document's `data_origin` marker pointed at `'real'`, one review's aspect
jsonb emptied, every concrete-aspect review rewritten to a bare opinion, a favourite filed under
`'restaurant'`, one fact sourced to `'walked past and looked'`, and an offering made bookable for a
merchant with no active pool (falsifier_plants.py:786-828). Same rule as D126: one statement, checks ON,
no `SET LOCAL`, no ghost id.

**Decision (a): eight of the nine aimed arms reddened their assertion, and one arm minted a name that
died with its transaction -- the registry refused the file for it.** The favourites arm's write also
made the reference census emit `orphan: favorites.restaurant`, because that family assembles its names
from the *values* it finds; the row was filed, and step 11 then read the registry against the plane and
answered `RESULT: FAIL -- the registry is inconsistent with the gate`. After rollback the plane does not
carry that name, so no witness can. The row was taken back -- registry 267 → **293 rows**, not the 294
the drive emitted -- and the arm's honest witness is the one it names,
`favourite subject_type is one the API can save`. This is D105's class arriving inside the registry, and
the reader caught it rather than my reading of it: a plant must not file an assertion whose identity is
a function of the data the plant itself wrote.

**Decision (b): `collections/guides reference live merchants` reads a jsonb key the seed never writes.**
The dropped arm was meant to write a ghost merchant id into a collection's items and the target stayed
green with no collateral, so the shape was counted: 4 collections, all 4 with an object at `items[0]`,
**0 items carrying `merchant_id` anywhere** -- the keys the seed actually writes are `note`,
`subject_id`, `subject_type` (the check is quality.sql:1002-1007). The predicate is therefore vacuous on
the artifact, and no legal write aimed at the shape the check assumes reaches it: an FK column cannot
touch it, because nothing in the schema claims those ids inside a jsonb array. Kept on the 23, reported.

**Decision (c): D126's blind-census finding closed from the other side.** The invented type on
`feedback_events` slid past `no unlisted type rides in the seeded data` (an unarmed pair), while the
invented type on `favorites` -- an armed pair -- reddened exactly that row, and it now carries a
witness. So the row is not broken, it is scoped: it guards the pairs the registry arms, which is what
its own name quietly promises and what this pair of arms measured from both sides.

**Numbers.** Arms 136 → **144**; harness `c8c2f84`. Pre-flight: 20 arms (the D126 family re-run plus the
nine new), 22 sessions, 19 hit, 1 green → dropped (decision (b)). Full drive: **144 arms + the control,
147 sessions, RESULT PASS** -- every target RED, nothing undeclared, closing baseline 216 / 0 identical
to opening, `quality.sql` md5 `4d3a707eff55971b0a2198e2a1b56777` unchanged. Registry 267 → **293 rows**
(27 emitted, 1 taken back per decision (a); 8 from an arm's own RED row, 19 from collateral). Coverage
183 → **193 of 216 (89.4%)**; witness kinds 254 commit + 39 file; step 11 PASS. Unwitnessed 33 → **23**.
Mechanism mix, measured from plant text: with the phantom row counted, 194 names / 91 with a witness
that switches nothing off / 103 with only switching witnesses; after taking it back, **193 / 90 / 103**
-- so three units of legal writes moved the non-switching half from 80 to 90 and the role-switch-only
group has stopped shrinking, because 103 of them are the `fk: ` family, whose plant is a dangling
reference by definition.

**Limits.** (i) Same as D126: a legal write is not an application trace; it says the assertion can be
lost to something the database accepts. (ii) 19 of the 27 rows are companions witnessed under a write
that also breaks the target, so they testify that a companion notices, not that the companion's own risk
case is reachable. (iii) The `every column that cannot vary…` row reddened 10 times in this family for
the reason §134 records -- its demand list is derived from data -- and the rating arms likewise moved
the counters and the rating-fact rows; those are scope-change witnesses. (iv) The count above is taken

**next.** (a) 23 left and they are now three named kinds: 8 rows about the registry and catalogues
