## D128 The last 23 rows sorted by what could possibly falsify them -- nine are data, ten need a migration, one is vacuous, two wait on #75 — 2026-09-27

Three units of plants (D125's 48, D126's 11, D127's 8) took the registry from 116 witnessed names to 193
and left 23. A queue that size invites "more of the same", but every arm this lane has shipped writes
data, and reading the 23 against their own SQL shows most of them cannot be lost that way. This unit
plants nothing; it decides what each row would take, so the queue stops being a count and becomes named
planes.

**Decision (a): nine are falsifiable from the data plane and are the next batch's real aim.**
`a join-one-type waiver is only true while the table ships one type` (quality.sql:1208-1213) is the one
row whose own detail text advertises the date it will go red -- the predicate is `c.types_n > 1` over the
data-derived `ref_cat`, so a single legal INSERT of a second subject type falsifies it, the shape D127's
favourites arm used. Two catalogue floors, `the reference census reads the catalogue`
(`count(*) FROM ref_cat >= 17`, :1178-1180) and `the polymorphic-pair census reads the catalogue`
(:1263), fall the other way: writes only add pairs, so these need a DELETE taking a counted pair to zero
rows -- D120 already planted that mechanism for a different row. Five demand-list rows --
`a bounded string column is answered by name` (:3022), `the string census declares a reading for every
type it catches` (:3104), `a census that folds case reports both readings…` (:3134),
`the elements of an object-array column all carry the same keys` (:2015) and
`a served view answers every column it exposes` (:3324) -- enumerate from the rows, which §134/§135
already proved experimentally: those arms reddened the cannot-vary, array and jsonb census rows 48, 7 and
7 times just by adding data. And `density: >= 300 merchants within 3km of Sha Tin` is a threshold over
lat/lng, so a legal mass UPDATE of coordinates reaches it.

**Decision (b): ten cannot be lost from data, and naming the input each reads is the whole point.**
`the registry names no column the schema has lost` (:1198), `the pairs declared probed are pairs the
schema has` (:1270), `an armed type resolves in a table the schema has` (:1410),
`a no-referent waiver still names a table the schema lacks` (:1425),
`a probe arm is a declared type and every armed type has an arm` (:1401),
`traffic sweep reaches the whole closure, not a hand list` (:257),
`a CHECK-bounded column is a door vocabulary too` (:2836), `a door vocabulary names a column the schema
has` (:2770), `every boolean that claims a verification is answered for its evidence` (:2156) and
`price_updated_at present for priced offerings` (:482) compare `pg_constraint`, `to_regclass`, column
lists, or `quality.sql`'s own hand-written `ref_registry` (:1150-1176) against the data. Reddening one
means dropping a column, shipping a table, adding a CHECK, or editing the hand list -- a migration or the
file under test, not a row. Two consequences are recorded rather than argued: a plant for any of these
would have to edit `data/seed/quality.sql`, another lane's working copy; and where the row's *other* side
is that same hand list, both sides of the gate are written by the gate -- so a green there proves the
file agrees with itself, and the honest verdict is "no data-plane witness exists", not "covered".

**Decision (c): one row is vacuous in a way no plant can fix, and two wait on another lane.**
`collections/guides reference live merchants` (:1002-1007) reads `it->>'merchant_id'` from collection
items; D127 counted 4 collections, 4 with an object at `items[0]`, and 0 items carrying that key anywhere
(`note`, `subject_id`, `subject_type` are what the seed writes). Its PASS says nothing about referential
integrity; the fix is to point the row at the keys that exist, which is another lane's edit.
`fk: share_links.created_by` and `fk: share_links.tenant_id` wait on #75 -- the migration creating the
table is uncommitted, so a witness there could not reopen from the committed tree.

**Numbers.** Nothing shipped changed: no gate file, checker, migration, harness or registry row -- the

## D129 Aiming is the test of a classification: nine "data-reachable" rows became two, and the seven that fell away say more than the arms that survived — 2026-09-27

§137 sorted the last 23 unwitnessed rows by reading the predicate behind each name, and put nine of them
on the data plane. This unit went to plant those nine. Writing an arm forces a second kind of reading --
not what the predicate says, but what its lists are built *from* -- and seven of the nine did not survive
it. Two arms remain, both legal writes, and the corrections are the entry.

**Decision (a): four of the nine are catalogue-derived, one is vacuous by registration, one is forbidden
by a unique index, one still needs an inventory nobody has taken.**
  - `a join-one-type waiver is only true while the table ships one type` (quality.sql:1208-1213) is the
    clearest: its predicate is `ref_registry JOIN ref_cat … WHERE r.kind = 'join-one-type' AND
    c.types_n > 1`, and the file registers exactly one INSERT into `ref_registry` (:1150-1176), whose
    kinds are `probe` and `not-a-reference`. No waiver of that kind exists, so the row is true over the
    empty set and its own detail says `no waiver of that kind is registered`. It is not awaiting a
    plant; it is awaiting a waiver nobody has written.
  - `the reference census reads the catalogue` (`count(*) FROM ref_cat >= 17`, :1178-1180) and
    `the polymorphic-pair census reads the catalogue` (:1263) count COLUMNS: `ref_cat` is filled by a
    loop over `pg_attribute` (:1119-1141), one row per unconstrained `*_id`/`*_by` column, whatever
    those columns carry. A DELETE cannot shrink a column list, so the floor falls only to a migration --
    §137's reasoning ("writes only add pairs, so these need a DELETE taking a pair to zero") was wrong
    about the unit the census counts.
  - `the string census declares a reading for every type it catches` (:3104) compares the hand-written
    `str_type` list against base types caught from the catalogues -- a new column type, not a new value.
  - `a census that folds case reports both readings and which one the demo exercises` (:3134) watches
    for a column whose distinct count differs between the folded and unfolded readings, i.e. two values
    differing only by case. The only citext columns are `users.email` and `users_email_tenant_uniq.email`
    -- and a unique index over a case-insensitive type is precisely the constraint that forbids such a
    pair. The row is guarded by a schema object on the same column it measures.
  - `a bounded string column is answered by name` (:3022) genuinely is a data-plane target -- collapse a
    many-distinct text column into the window (≤ 12 distinct, ≥ 20 rows, ≤ 1 value per 4 rows) and the
    demand list gains an unanswered entry -- but the first candidate measured (`locations.address`) does
    not exist, so the arm waits for a column inventory rather than a guess. Left open on purpose.

**Decision (b): the plant cannot call the gate's own helpers, so geometry has to be stated in the plant's
own terms.** `density: >= N merchants within 3km of Sha Tin` (:524-529) decides by
`pg_temp.haversine_m(22.3831, 114.1876, lat, lng) <= 3000`, and that function exists only while
`quality.sql` runs -- the plant executes before the gate body, so it cannot call it. The ring is
therefore reproduced as a bounding box from the same centroid (±0.027° lat, ±0.0292° lng at 22.4° N), and
the destination (22.20, 114.30) was chosen INSIDE the Hong Kong bbox :531-535 guards, so the row that goes
red is the density row and not the one that says every coordinate is in the territory. That is a claim
about the geometry, and the pre-flight is what tests it: the density row reddened, the bbox row did not
appear among the collateral.

**Decision (c): two arms survived, and both are legal writes.** One merchant's first `images` element is
given a `source` key none of the other 520 merchants' elements carry -- all of them hold exactly `alt`,

## D130 The drive now refuses to file a witness for an assertion the unmutated gate does not file, so the reader's invariant became a precondition — 2026-09-27

§136 recorded the first time `check_falsifier_registry.mjs` refused this lane's file: a plant that files a
favourite under an invented subject type also makes the reference census emit
`orphan: favorites.restaurant`, because that family builds its names from the values it finds, and after
`ROLLBACK` no such assertion is on the plane. The row was deleted. D129's drive minted it again under a
new unit, and the drive's own summary line counted it as a novel name -- so the deletion was never a fix,
only a re-finding of the same hole one batch later.

**Decision (a): the refusal belongs in the emission, and the drive already holds the fact it needs.** The
first session of every run is unmutated, and its name list is what the report protocol carries back as
the `N|` row and the loop passes onward as `expect`. So the filter is two lines at the one place rows are
built (falsifier_plants.py:1051-1075): a candidate row is dropped unless its assertion name is in the
baseline plane, and the summary prints what it refused. `orphan: favorites.restaurant` was the only name
in the fleet that fell to it -- every other name this lane files was named by a `qc` INSERT before any
plant ran.

**Decision (b): the plant still shows what it showed; only the filing changes.** Re-running the minting
arm alone gives the identical verdict -- target `favourite subject_type is one the API can save` RED, one
collateral named, closing baseline 216 assertions / 0 red -- while appending **0** rows and printing
`refused 1 name(s) the unmutated gate does not file: orphan: favorites.restaurant`. That distinction is
the point of the whole unit: the reference census noticing an invented type is a real observation about
the gate and it stays in the arm's text; it is not a demonstration that an assertion which exists can
fail, and the registry holds only the second kind of claim.

**Decision (c): an invariant moved from audit to precondition.** Step 11 reads the registry against the
plane and answered FAIL twice; after this change the harness cannot produce the file it refuses. The
second gain is arithmetic that used to land on the reader: D129 printed "3 novel names" where 2 were on
the plane, and a future drive's summary now prints the refusal beside the append count.

**Numbers.** Harness `aca885b`; no assertion, arm, gate file or migration changed. Targeted re-run of the
minting arm: 3 sessions, RESULT PASS, appended 0, refused 1. Full regression drive: **146 arms + the control, 149 whole-gate
sessions, RESULT PASS**, every arm reddening its own assertion, **11 rows appended** against a 327-line
copy of the registry -- 0 from an arm's own RED row and 0 naming an assertion that carried no witness
before, so all 11 are second witnesses for (check, arm) pairs the fleet had never filed together -- plus
the same single refusal. Registry 306 -> **317 rows**, coverage unchanged at **195 of 216 (90.3%)**,
21 unwitnessed; `quality.sql` md5 `4d3a707eff55971b0a2198e2a1b56777` before
and after.

**Limits.** (i) The filter's denominator is this working copy's plane -- 216 assertions, two of them from
another lane's uncommitted migration (#75) -- so it refuses plant-minted names, not names belonging to
another stream. (ii) A data-derived name that is also on the baseline plane stays witnessable:
`orphan: favorites.merchant` is assembled by the same census from a value the seed really writes, and
D120's witness for it stands. The line is "was this assertion filed before the plant ran", which is
exactly the reproducibility requirement. (iii) The per-arm table still lists minted names as collateral,
and should -- they were reddened -- so the ledger keeps reading collateral as observation.

**next.** (a) D131: the two plantable rows left -- `a bounded string column is answered by name`, which

## D131 The last plantable row is planted, and the one that looked plantable turns out to have a demand list written in SQL, not in data — 2026-09-27

D129 reduced the queue to two candidates: `a bounded string column is answered by name` and
`a served view answers every column it exposes`. This unit settles both -- one becomes a witness, the
other becomes a disposition -- and the difference was decided by reading what each census enumerates
over.

**Decision (a): the bounded-string row is data's, and the arm is a collapse.** Its predicate (
quality.sql:3022-3030) is `vocab_win NOT IN vocab_answer`, where `vocab_win` is derived from the rows:
a string column with <= 12 distinct values over >= 20 rows and <= 1 value per 4 rows. So a column can
*enter* the window by a write, and an answer that exists for the old window members says nothing about
the newcomer. The arm takes `documents.title` -- 1040 rows over 934 distinct values, no CHECK, no unique
index, absent from the answer list -- and folds it into 12 buckets (falsifier_plants.py:877-880,
committed 43091a2):

    UPDATE documents SET title = 'plant bucket ' || (abs(hashtext(title)) % 12);

Pre-flight: 3 whole-gate sessions, target RED, **zero collateral** -- the cleanest single-row witness
this lane has filed, because the write touches a column no companion reads. Coverage after the drive:
**196 of 216 (90.7%)**.

**Decision (b): the served-view row cannot be reached from data, and the reason is structural.** Its
predicate (quality.sql:3324-3340) is `view_data NOT IN view_answer` matched on `(vw, col)` -- the demand
list is the set of columns the shipped views expose, which is fixed by their definitions in the
migration set, while the *counts* come from the rows. A write can change a column's derived kind (the
`const` -> `sparse` move the exemption text at :3318-3323 advertises, and which
`a view kind is exercised or exempted` and `a view answer names the kind the census derives` do notice --
both already witnessed), but no write adds a column a view does not have. So the row joins the
catalogue-bound group: falsifiable only by a migration that widens a view.

**Measurement (c): the arm that would have tested it was dropped because the schema refused the guess.**
The exemption says "events for 260 of 520 merchants puts `v_merchant_funnel.views` at 2 values over 520
rows", and the obvious `INSERT INTO events (tenant_id, merchant_id, …)` aborted at the pre-flight:
**`events` has no merchant_id column**. The funnel reaches a merchant through the polymorphic pair
instead -- `WHERE e.subject_type = 'merchant' … GROUP BY e.subject_id`, with the counter keyed on
`e.name IN ('view','click','reserve','cart_add')`. That is written down for two reasons: it is the fact
the next traffic-shaped arm needs, and it shows the exemption text naming a measurement (`260 merchants`)
rather than the column the measurement actually rides on.

**Numbers.** Arms 146 -> **147** (one added, one dropped after aborting); harness `43091a2`. Pre-flight:
3 sessions for the collapse arm (PASS), 2 sessions for the events arm (run unread -> removed). Full
drive: **150 whole-gate sessions, RESULT PASS**, 9 rows appended against a 338-line copy of the
registry, closing baseline 216 assertions / 0 red. Registry 317 -> **326 rows**; coverage 195 -> **196 of 216
(90.7)**; unwitnessed 21 -> **20**. `quality.sql` md5 `4d3a707eff55971b0a2198e2a1b56777` unchanged.

**Limits.** (i) The collapse arm's RED is a witness that the census notices an unlabelled bounded column;
it is not a claim that the demo ships collapsed titles. (ii) D126's limit stands for every legal-write
witness: the database accepts the write, which is not the same as an endpoint performing it. (iii) The
served-view disposition is a claim about which set the predicate enumerates over -- the (vw, col) pairs
-- and would be falsified by a view that gains a column from data, which SQL does not do.

**next.** (a) 20 unwitnessed names, of which none is now plantable from data: the catalogue-bound
group, the vacuous-by-construction group (`collections/guides reference live merchants`, the
join-one-type waiver), the NOT NULL-implied row, the citext-indexed row, the 2 share_links names (#75),
and the ones needing a migration. (b) Write the per-row disposition into TRACEABILITY or a short section
so the queue reads as closed-by-kind rather than as pending work. (c) #71, eleventh time standing on it.
(d) Carried: #75, #62, #64, #58, #44, #17, #19, #34, #79, #80, step 11's `--registry` percentage residue,
§87's session-time-zone seam, D91's served leg, §130's missing `guide` branch.

## D132 The twenty rows this lane will not plant, named one by one with the reason each one has -- closing the falsification arc by kind rather than by count — 2026-09-27

D131 planted the last row the queue believed was reachable, which left 20 and no candidate mechanism. A
queue in that state should be closed by naming each row, not by shrinking the claim, because "we ran out
of ideas" and "these are not the data plane's" read identically a month later. Each line below is the
shipped predicate plus what it enumerates over, all citations from the working copy of
`data/seed/quality.sql`.

**Six need a schema change, not a write.** `a CHECK-bounded column is a door vocabulary too` (:2836) and
`a door vocabulary names a column the schema has` (:2770) read `pg_constraint`; `a no-referent waiver
still names a table the schema lacks` (:1425) and `an armed type resolves in a table the schema has`
(:1410) read `to_regclass` -- the first goes red the day someone ships the table it says is absent, and
its own comment says the waiver must then be re-argued; `every boolean that claims a verification is
answered for its evidence` (:2156) enumerates boolean columns; `traffic sweep reaches the whole closure,
not a hand list` (:257) counts the closure `pg_constraint` yields. None of these can be moved by a row.

**Nine have both sides written inside the gate's own file.** `the reference census reads the catalogue`
(`count(*) FROM ref_cat >= 17`, built at :1119-1141, asserted at :1178-1180) and
`the polymorphic-pair census reads the catalogue` (:1263) enumerate COLUMNS from `pg_attribute`;
`the registry names no column the schema has lost` (:1198), `the pairs declared probed are pairs the
schema has` (:1270), `the arm registry agrees with the probed-pair counts` (:1462),
`a probe arm is a declared type and every armed type has an arm` (:1401) and
`a join-one-type waiver is only true while the table ships one type` (:1208-1213) compare the data
against the hand-written `ref_registry` and `poly_vocab` lists at :1150-1176 -- and the join-one-type row
additionally polices a waiver kind the file never registers, so it is true over an empty set and prints
`no waiver of that kind is registered`; `the string census declares a reading for every type it catches`
(:3104) compares the hand `str_type` list against `pg_type`; and
`a served view answers every column it exposes` (:3324-3340) matches on the (view, column) pairs that the
shipped view definitions fix. For all nine, a plant would have to edit the file under test, and a green
there proves the file agrees with itself -- worth saying out loud about a gate even when it is this
lane's own ledger.

**Three are true because the schema or the seed forbids the state they watch for.**
`price_updated_at present for priced offerings` (:482): `offerings.price_updated_at` is NOT NULL and a
role switch does not silence NOT NULL, so no data state falsifies it.
`a census that folds case reports both readings and which one the demo exercises` (:3134): its red needs
two citext values differing only by case, and the only citext columns are `users.email` behind
`users_email_tenant_uniq`, a unique index over a case-insensitive type that forbids exactly that pair.
`collections/guides reference live merchants` (:1002-1007): it reads `it->>'merchant_id'` and the seed
writes no such key into any collection item -- §136 counted 0 of 4 collections, the item keys being
`note`, `subject_id`, `subject_type` -- so its PASS is not evidence about references at all, and the
finding belongs to the file's owner rather than to this queue.

**Two wait on another lane.** `fk: share_links.created_by -> users.id` and
`fk: share_links.tenant_id -> tenants.id` exist only on the uncommitted `V7__share_links.sql` (#75); on a
database built from HEAD they are red for a reason this lane does not own (D108), which is also why they
cannot be witnessed from this working copy without describing another stream's artifact.

**Numbers.** Nothing shipped changed -- no harness, arm, registry row or gate file -- and no session
touched the database. The registry stands at **326 rows, 196 of 216 assertions witnessed (90.7%), 20
unwitnessed** (step 11 PASS on `nexus_gate_283340_1790454442`), the fleet at **147 arms** (`43091a2`).
Across the arc since D123 the registry went 116 -> 326 rows and 87 -> 196 witnessed names; of those 196,
93 have at least one witness whose plant switches no check off, and the remainder are essentially the
`fk: ` family, whose witness is a dangling reference by definition. The residue resolves as
6 + 9 + 3 + 2 = 20, with no row counted twice.

**Limits.** (i) This is a disposition, not a measurement: each claim is a predicate read together with an
earlier unit's experiment (§134's demand-list growth, §136's item-key count, §138's refusal), and nothing
was re-derived by a new plant, because none was possible. (ii) "No data-plane witness exists" is a claim
about this lane's mechanism set: a schema-plane falsifier (mutating the schema inside a rolled-back
session) could reach the six, and a file-plane falsifier the nine -- different harnesses, different risks,
neither built. (iii) The three forbidden-state rows are the interesting ones for the gate's owner: a row
that no admitted state can redden is documentation wearing a check's clothes.

**next.** (a) The lane's remaining product is either those two harnesses or a decision not to build them;

## D133 Nine citations I had accused of being wrong are right, and the file that misled me is the mapping table -- `TRACEABILITY.md`'s § column is not the spec's — 2026-09-27

Task #79 has carried this sentence since D116: "nine sites use bare `§106` to describe
deletion/retention and they cite the wrong TRACEABILITY requirement row: row 106 is *AI transparency*,
the row they mean is 100." It was written from `docs/TRACEABILITY.md` -- a table whose first column is
headed `§` and whose line 1 declares "§ numbering = `新建 文本文档.txt`" -- and never from the file it
declares. This unit reads that file, and the claim collapses.

**Decision (a): the nine sites are correct, in the plane they were written in.** The spec numbers its own
top-level sections, and at `新建 文本文档.txt:2773` the heading is **`# 106. Privacy`**, followed by
`# 107. Merchant Data Ownership` (:2793) and `# 108. AI Transparency` (:2807). So
`IdentityRepository.java:106/339/360`, `MeController.java:33/111/122/125`,
`ConfigDecorationTest.java:27/52` and `application.yml:100` -- all writing `§106` about erasure,
deletion-request bookkeeping and export -- cite the section that is about exactly that. So do the four
design docs I also put on the list: `DATABASE.md:191` ("`deletion_requests` — §106 data-retention
workflow"), `API_CONTRACT.md:193` ("DELETE `/api/v1/me` creates `deletion_request` (§106)"),
`CONSUMER.md:59` ("## 9. Privacy & data rights (§106)") and `SECURITY.md:57`. The convention is the one
`quality.sql` uses out loud ("spec §55", "§94 cold-start density"): a bare `§NN` names a spec section,
and the ledger citation reader lists `§NN` among the things that are *not* file citations
(§120's own accounting).

**Decision (b): the mapping table's § column does not carry the spec's numbers in this band, and that is
the defect worth reporting.** Comparing `TRACEABILITY.md`'s rows with the spec headings in the 96-110
window, **0 of 13 comparable rows agree**: TRACE row 100 is "Privacy: export/delete/reset; merchant data
ownership" (spec §106 + §107), row 101 is i18n (spec §111), 102 Reliability (spec §104), 103 AI failure
ladder (spec §105), 104 Caching (spec §103), 105 No fake reviews/traffic (spec §109/§110), 106 AI
transparency (spec §108), 107 legal/compliance, 108 one-command dev env, 109 CI/CD, 110 git discipline
(spec §109-§115 name none of those in those positions), and rows 98/99 are absent while the spec has
`98. Data Flywheel` and `99. Feedback` there. The table's own header therefore over-claims: it says its
numbering *is* the spec's, and in this band it is an independent sequence. That single line is what made
nine correct citations look off by six and would have sent a fix through them that broke them.

**Decision (c): what is actually still broken is narrower and already machine-checked.** Two sites spell
the plane, and there the plane is wrong: `CollectionsController.java:186` and
`CollectionsReadTest.java:188` both write `STATUS §106`, and STATUS has no `## 106. ` heading that means
them -- `node scripts/check_status_citations.mjs` still exits FAIL naming exactly those two today, with
`STATUS §28` and `STATUS §66` reported ok in the same run. The fix is theirs to make (both files are
another lane's working copy); what the reader needs from this unit is nothing -- it already refuses the
right thing, and this is the second time it has caught a claim my prose had already accepted.

**Measurement note (d), which re-scopes #80.** The 81-token residue that task #80 wants "re-aimed" is
probably not a residue of errors: if a bare `§NN` is a spec citation, most of those tokens are correctly
pointing at a document that is not STATUS, and re-aiming them at ledger sections would be the actual
defect. #80's first sub-question -- "does any document define section 106 for the deletion/retention
workflow?" -- is answered **yes, at `新建 文本文档.txt:2773`**, and the task is re-scoped to
counting how many of the 81 are spec-plane (correct) rather than ledger-plane (checkable), not re-aiming
all of them.

**Numbers.** Nothing shipped changed: no gate file, checker, harness, registry row or another lane's file
was touched, and no session opened the database. The registry stands at 326 rows / 196 of 216 witnessed
(90.7%); `check_status_citations.mjs` reports **4 spelled citations outside a code span, 2 resolving, 14
mentions inside spans, 2 BAD**, over 565 scanned files at a HEAD where STATUS holds 109 headings (§23 to
§141). The evidence read for this entry: `新建 文本文档.txt` is 4,340 lines with `# NN. Title` headings;
`docs/TRACEABILITY.md` rows 96-110 (13 rows compared, 0 matching); the 13 citing sites listed above.

**Limits.** (i) The 0-of-13 comparison covers the 96-110 band, which is where the accusation lived; the
rest of TRACEABILITY's § column is not audited here, so the claim is "not in this band", not "never".
(ii) `# 106. Privacy` is read from the spec's own heading text; whether the spec's *content* under it
covers export/delete/reset was not compared line by line. (iii) The four design docs and the Java sites
are cited from `grep` output with the file paths as the reader prints them (`services/platform/...`);
task #79's text abbreviated them to `apps/platform/...`, which is another small way a remembered path
differs from a measured one.

**next.** (a) #79 is rewritten: report the two `STATUS §106` sites and the `TRACEABILITY.md:1` over-claim;
withdraw the nine-and-four accusation. (b) #80 re-scoped as (d) says: classify the 81 by plane before
touching any of them. (c) The rule this unit exists to leave behind: **when a citation looks off by a
constant, read the file that defines the numbering, not the table that maps it** -- an off-by-N that
appears in a mapping table is usually the table's, and "fixing" the citations propagates it. (d) #71,

step 11's `--registry` percentage residue, §87's session-time-zone seam, D91's served leg, §130's

## D134 The whole shipped gate, run end to end on a from-scratch database, with the two-plane consequence spelled out — 2026-09-27

Ten commits of registry and ledger work (D124-D133) had each been checked reader by reader -- step 8,
step 9, step 10, step 11 run by hand against the working copy. That is the lane's habit, but it leaves
one question unanswered: does the gate as shipped still pass from nothing? This unit runs
`scripts/db_gate_fresh.sh` and reports what the eleven steps said.

**Decision (a): run it for real, and skip only the step that would write another lane's files.**
`--skip-generate` was passed, so step 3 did not regenerate `data/seed/out/` and the fresh database was
loaded from the CSVs as they stand on disk. The reason is the shared-tree rule, not convenience: the
working copy carries another stream's uncommitted edits (quality.sql, four contract docs, a V7
migration), and a generator run would overwrite generated artifacts this lane does not own. The rest of
the script ran unchanged: it created `nexus_gate_336563_1790480323` from `template0`, applied
`infra/db/migrations/V*.sql` + `00_roles.sql`, loaded the seed, gated it, probed the truncate guard, and
dropped the database at the end. **Exit 0, all eleven steps PASS**, closing with "216 quality checks on a
from-scratch schema (tables=58, migrations=7)".

**Decision (b): `migrations=7` is the two-plane claim from D107/D108, now demonstrated by the shipped
script rather than asserted in prose.** A from-scratch build of THIS working copy applies seven
migrations and files 216 assertions -- including the `share_links` ones -- because
`V7__share_links.sql` exists on disk while remaining uncommitted (#75). So the green this lane reports
every session is a green of the working copy, and a checkout at HEAD would build six migrations and
214 checks with two reds, which is what D107/D108 measured on a clean worktree. Two consequences are
recorded rather than argued: the seed gate is currently coupled to another lane's uncommitted file, and
any claim of the form "the gate is green" has to name its plane. This unit did not re-run the HEAD plane
(it needs a separate checkout and another full build); it cites D107/D108 for that number and flags it
as the obvious next verification, not as something re-confirmed today.

**Numbers.** Steps and verdicts as the script printed them: 1 create, 2 migrations+roles, 3 skipped by
flag, 4 load, 5 `quality.sql` -- 216 checks, 0 red; 6 truncate probe PASS ("the empty child is cleared,
the child with rows refuses by name, and the refusal costs nothing"); 7 jsonb reads PASS; 8
`check_ledger_citations.mjs --worktree` PASS; 9 `check_comment_citations.mjs` PASS -- **73 comment-plane
citations across 21 files**, up from 70 before D125-D131 were written, i.e. the new arms' own comments are
being resolved; 10 `check_ledger_sections.mjs` PASS; 11 `check_falsifier_registry.mjs` PASS over **326
rows**, every row naming a live assertion and an openable witness. Registry, harness and docs were not
modified by this unit.

**Limits.** (i) With step 3 skipped, this run does NOT prove the generator agrees with the current
schema -- that is exactly the defect class D21/D62 built the script to surface (a fresh deploy dying on
first load), and it remains unproven today. The generator's own FK self-check would be the thing to
trust, and it was not run. (ii) The fresh database was built from the working copy's migration
directory, so its green is a working-copy green, not a HEAD green. (iii) One run, one container, no
concurrency: other lanes may have been writing during it, and the run reads their files as found.

**next.** (a) Re-run the gate WITH generation once `data/seed/out/` is unowned-and-clean or the owning
lane agrees, so step 3's self-check is back in the evidence. (b) Re-measure the HEAD plane (a clean
checkout, expected 6 migrations / 214 checks / 2 reds per D107-D108) and file it as a number rather than
a remembered one. (c) #71, #75, #91, #79, #80 unchanged; carried list unchanged.

D134 named two gaps in its own evidence: step 3 had been skipped, and the HEAD numbers were quoted from

script with no flags: it regenerated `data/seed/out/` (a gitignored directory, so no tracked file was

all eleven steps -- `RESULT: PASS -- 216 quality checks on a from-scratch schema (tables=58,
migrations=7)`, exit 0, with generate.py's own FK-integrity self-check reading `PASS (FK integrity,
bounds, naming, density, language mix)` and the truncate probe reporting `49 table(s) cleared -- 49
named by generate.py, 0 found by the schema's own foreign keys`. That is the D62/D63 defect class actively
ruled out for today's schema, which is what step 3 skipping had left open.

**Measurement (b): HEAD is still red, and the two reds are the same two.** Run 2 executed the same script
inside a detached worktree of HEAD (`git worktree add --detach`, removed afterwards; `git worktree list`

a tail dump (21 in this transcript), so "214 assertions at HEAD" is not derivable from this run. It had

## D136 The §-citation "residue" is two deliberate fake fixtures and the real defect is that 1,253 of 1,353 bare citations are ambiguous by construction — 2026-09-27

Task #80 inherited a number from D116: 1,100 `§N` tokens in the ledgers, 528 non-resolving, 81 surviving
after the recovered-title brackets are excluded, "to be split by reading each one". D133 broke the premise
under it -- if a bare `§NN` names a section of the product spec, most of those tokens were never broken.
This unit counts instead of reading one by one, over a fresh census of both ledgers.

**Grammar, because the count is nothing without it.** A token is `§` plus 1-3 digits, optionally a range
(second number folded into the same token); lines are scanned twice, once with inline code spans stripped
("outside", where a citation is a claim) and once as written ("inside", where the shipped readers report
mentions and do not judge them). A number resolves in a plane if the plane has that heading: **SPEC** =
`# NN. Title` in `新建 文本文档.txt` (173 headings, up to 172), **STATUS** = `## NN. ` in
`docs/STATUS.md` (112), **DECISION** = `## DNN ` in `docs/DECISIONS.md` (123). A token is ambiguous when
its number exists in more than one of those.

**Result: there is no residue, and there is an ambiguity problem nobody had measured.** 1,900 tokens:
1,353 outside a code span, 547 inside one. Outside a span, **1,253 (92.6%) resolve in two or three
planes** -- 772 in all three, 455 in SPEC+DECISION, 26 in SPEC+STATUS -- while **98 (7.2%) are
unambiguously SPEC and zero are unambiguously STATUS-only or DECISION-only**. The remaining 2 are
`§99999`, which is not residue but a deliberate negative fixture: it appears inside the falsifier text
that proves `check_status_citations.mjs` reddens a citation to a section that does not exist
(STATUS §126's "a citation to §99999 (exit 1)"), and my 3-digit regex clipped it to `§999`. So the
81-token queue in #80 is not a queue of errors: the ledgers already use the spec plane as the default
referent for a bare `§NN`, which is what D133 found when it checked §106 against the spec.

**Decision (a): do not wire a guard for this, and record the reason.** An arm that refuses ambiguous bare
citations would be red on 1,253 tokens on the day it ships, which is D116's stated failure mode for new
guards ("a guard that is red on day one gets ignored by day two"). The useful asymmetry is that the
readers already judge the only form that *cannot* be ambiguous: a spelled plane. Those forms are
counted here at **20 `STATUS §NN`** across the two ledgers and **21 `spec §NN`** across docs and
`quality.sql` -- small, and every one of them checkable, which is the property the 1,900 bare tokens
lack.

**Decision (b): the convention is stated where it will be read, not retro-fitted.** Going forward, a
ledger citation meant as a ledger pointer spells its plane (`STATUS §121`, `D133`), and a bare `§NN` is
read as the spec unless context says otherwise. That is what §142's retraction, §141's dispositions and
the `spec §55` / `§94` comments in `quality.sql` have all been doing implicitly; writing it down is the
cheapest fix available, because the alternative -- disambiguating 1,253 historical tokens -- would churn
every paragraph this lane has ever cited and would silently convert spec citations into ledger ones.

**Numbers.** Script: `.../nexus-d63/plane_census.py`, run over the two ledgers as of `ceffeb9`
(STATUS through §144, DECISIONS through D135). Counts above; per-section attribution shows the heaviest
writers as the preamble (192 tokens), STATUS §123 (137), D115 (87), STATUS §124/§125 (69 each), which are
the recovery-era sections D116 already flagged as verbatim-by-choice. Nothing shipped changed: no gate
file, checker, harness or registry row, and no ledger citation was rewritten by this unit.

**Limits.** (i) Resolution is existence, not intent: `§106` in `CollectionsController.java`'s
`STATUS §106` is both a STATUS-106 non-heading and a SPEC-106 section, and only the spelled prefix tells
you which was meant -- which is the whole argument of this unit, and why 2 real BADs survive (D133).
(ii) Ranges are counted once and attributed by their first number, so `§101-§108` is a SPEC+STATUS+DECISION
token, not two. (iii) The 3-digit cap in the regex mis-clipped `§99999`; fixed by recognizing it as a
fixture rather than by re-running, since the count of such cases is 2 and both are named here.

**next.** (a) #80 closes: no residue to re-aim, and the ambiguity finding is recorded instead. (b) If a
guard is ever wanted, the honest shape is one that counts ambiguous bare tokens per new paragraph and
warns without failing, so history is not red. (c) #71, #75, #79, #62, #64, #58, #44, #17, #19, #34 and
the carried list stand as written.

## D137 #71, answered: `facts` is CHECK-free by design, and the measurement says why -- four of the lane's legal-write witnesses live in the space a CHECK would close — 2026-09-27

Task #71 has been re-stated eleven times: "`facts` is the only seeded table with no CHECK -- V8, or say
why not." This unit says why not, and the saying is a measurement rather than a preference.

**Measurement (a): what the table actually is.** 5,688 rows, six `attribute` values (price 2080, rating
1727, address 684, cuisine 520, opening_hours 520, capacity 157), three `subject_type` values (offering
2924, merchant 2080, location 684), `value` an object on every row (0 non-objects, 0 empty), `source`
never NULL and always inside the six documented provenance values, `expires_at` never NULL and later than
`observed_at` on all 5,688 rows. `pg_constraint` for the table returns exactly two entries:
`PRIMARY KEY (id)` and `FOREIGN KEY (merchant_id) REFERENCES merchants(id) ON DELETE CASCADE`. So every
invariant named above is currently enforced nowhere but the gate.

**Measurement (b): a candidate CHECK list, and the number that caught me writing it.** The obvious V8 is
`CHECK (jsonb_typeof(value) = 'object')`, `CHECK (source IN (…six…))`, `CHECK (expires_at > observed_at)`,
`CHECK (expires_at IS NOT NULL)`, `CHECK (attribute IN (…))`, `CHECK (subject_type IN (…))`. Counted
against the live data, the first four have **0 violations**, and the fifth would have too -- but my
guessed `subject_type` list omitted `location`, so the query reported 684 "violations" and those 684 rows
were exactly the address facts. That is the failure mode a CHECK turns a guess into: the seeder's own
`generate.py` FK self-check and this table's qc rows read the vocabulary from the schema or the data,
while a hand-authored `CHECK (… IN (…))` freezes whatever the author happened to list, and the load dies
on the day a seventh value appears. `merchant_categories` and friends already show what that costs: it is
why D105's three backstop constraints were named from `pg_constraint` rather than transcribed.

**Decision (c): the cost that settles it is falsification, not flexibility.** Four of the rows above are
asserted by qc rows whose ONLY witnesses are legal writes the schema itself accepts -- D126's arms
`one fact made timeless`, `one opening-hours fact given a 25-hour TTL`,
`one fact sourced to an undeclared string`, and `a price fact stamped with the hours TTL instead of the
six-hour one`, with `the §19 provenance axis and the §109 stamp axis stay separate on facts` carrying a
fifth. A CHECK silences none of those plants: `session_replication_role = replica` suppresses FKs and
triggers but not CHECKs or NOT NULLs, which is exactly why §135's `price_updated_at present for priced
offerings` became unfalsifiable once the column was NOT NULL. Shipping V8 with the four 0-violation
constraints would convert four demonstrated-failable assertions into rows no data state can redden --
documentation wearing a check's clothes, the category §141 spends three entries on. The lane's own end
state (196 of 216 witnessed, 20 explained by kind) would get worse on two axes at once: fewer witnessed
names, and more names with no possible witness.

**Decision (d): what would change the answer.** A CHECK earns its place where the gate has NO row, or
where the row's witness is a role switch that a CHECK would not have to defeat. `facts` has neither gap:
each invariant above has a live qc row, and each of those rows has a legal-write or declared-disappearance
witness already filed. If a future unit wants schema enforcement here, the honest version is the one that
derives its vocabulary from the catalogues -- and D105's three backstops are the precedent for what that
costs in flexibility.

**Numbers.** Facts plane: 5,688 rows / 6 attributes / 3 subject types / 0 non-object values / 0 NULL or
out-of-list `source` / 0 NULL `expires_at` / 0 non-future TTL, read from
`nexus_gate_283340_1790454442` (scratch `d137_facts.sql`, `d137_b.sql`); 5 facts-related qc rows with
13 witness rows total in `data/seed/falsifiers.tsv` (326 rows at `e450131`). No migration was written, no
tracked file outside the two ledgers changed, and no gate step was affected. #71 closes as answered --
"or say why not" being the option the task offered.

**Limits.** (i) The 0-violation counts are of THIS seed at THIS load; a CHECK's value is precisely to hold
when a future load differs, so this argument weighs the loss of falsifiability against a protection the qc
rows already provide per run -- it is not a claim that CHECKs are wrong in general. (ii) `value`'s internal
shape per attribute (which keys a price fact must carry) is enforced by D86's payload-shape census and was
not re-audited here. (iii) The 684-row false positive above is reported because it is the interesting
number in the measurement, not because the vocabulary question is settled -- the gate's door-vocabulary
rows are.

**next.** (a) The `facts` question is closed; re-open it only if a qc row covering one of these invariants
loses its witness, since that is the condition under which schema enforcement becomes the better trade.
(b) Carried: #73 (196 of 216), #75, #79, #62, #64, #58, #44, #17, #19, #34, step 11's `--registry`
percentage residue, §87's session-time-zone seam, D91's served leg, §130's missing `guide` branch.

## D139 The failure path now counts what it was reading, and the number it printed is not the one the ledger had been quoting — 2026-09-27

D135 recorded a small defect: `db_gate_fresh.sh` prints its assertion total when step 5 passes and prints
nothing of the sort when step 5 fails, so "214 assertions at HEAD" survived in three entries as a figure
inherited from D107/D108 rather than re-read. D138 had to refuse a claim for the same reason. This unit
fixes the reporting and then uses it.

**Decision (a): a failing gate reports the same census a passing one does.** The else-branch at
scripts/db_gate_fresh.sh:203-214 now counts `^  PASS` and `^  FAIL` lines from the same temp file it was
about to tail, and prints them with the two planes the schema was built on, before the last 25 lines --
so the reason a run stopped is legible without a second run to ask "how many were there?"

**Measurement (b): verified on the plane where it fires, not on a green one.** A detached worktree at
`944c0b1` (the commit before the share write), running the patched script with generation, reaches step 5
and dies there as expected: **"step 5 filed 212 assertion(s), 2 red (tables=57, migrations=6)"**, the two
reds being `a door vocabulary names a column the schema has` and `a CHECK-bounded column is a door
vocabulary too`, exit 1. The control is the same script on today's HEAD (`d7c2d57`), where step 5 passes
and prints **"216 quality checks"**, tables=58, migrations=7, and the failure has moved to step 7.

**Finding (c): the remembered number was stale by two.** Every entry from D107 onward quoted 214
assertions for a clean HEAD checkout; measured today at `944c0b1` it is **212**. Nothing about the schema
changed between a304947 and now that would add assertions -- the committed `quality.sql` has simply lost
two rows in the four months of ledger work since, and nobody re-counted because the plane that was red was
never re-run. That is the exact failure mode this script exists to prevent, arriving in the script's own
reporting: a total that only prints on success is a total that stops being true the moment anything else
moves, and the red plane -- the one people quote when they say "HEAD is red" -- is precisely the plane
where it never printed.

**Numbers.** One script hunk (12 lines, `scripts/db_gate_fresh.sh`), two full from-scratch runs of ~4
minutes each, both throwaway databases created and dropped by the scripts, one worktree added and removed;
`git worktree list` shows the main checkout only. Neither run opened the kept loaded seed
`nexus_gate_283340_1790454442`. Registry unchanged at 326 rows / 196 of 216.

**Limits.** (i) 212 is today's HEAD-plane count at `944c0b1`, not a constant; the point of the fix is that
the next such claim can be re-read instead of remembered. (ii) The success path's wording is unchanged, so
existing transcripts and step 11's parsing are unaffected -- verified by the control run printing the
familiar line. (iii) The failure path still exits at step 5, so a red gate reports nothing about steps
6-11; that is by design (a seed that fails its own gate should not certify citations), and it is why

## D140 A migration is not landed when it is committed; it is landed when every plane that runs it has it -- which the share write did not — 2026-09-27

D138 committed `V7__share_links.sql` with the share controller, repository and test, and recorded that
the test had not been run. This unit ran it, and the answer is not what the commit suggested.

**Measurement (a): the module compiles clean, and the test says otherwise.** `mvn -o -B clean
test-compile` in `services/platform` rebuilt 130 main and 41 test sources with BUILD SUCCESS --
`ShareController.class`, `ShareRepository.class` and `ShareLinkTest.class` all present. Then
`mvn -o -B test -Dtest=ShareLinkTest` ran **5 tests, 3 failures**, each an
`BadSqlGrammarException ... relation "share_links" does not exist`. So the feature is compiled, wired and
reachable over HTTP -- and its three database-touching corners are red, because the integration-test
database never received the migration this lane committed an hour earlier.

**Measurement (b): the gap is specific to one plane, and closing it is one command.** A fresh-database run
already has it (`db_gate_fresh.sh` applies `infra/db/migrations/V*.sql`, which is why HEAD reports 7
migrations and 216 checks), and `e2e_fresh.sh` builds its own. What no script rebuilds is the long-lived
`nexus_test` that surefire talks to. `NEXUS_DB_NAME=nexus_test
scripts/db_apply_migrations.sh --file infra/db/migrations/V7__share_links.sql` applied it -- one file,
additive, no re-run of V1-V6, no `--force` over anything already present -- and the same test command then
reported **Tests run: 5, Failures: 0, Errors: 0** with BUILD SUCCESS.

**Decision (c): what this lane now owes whenever it commits a migration.** A migration commit is two
planes: the from-scratch gate, which proves it builds, and each live database that is *not* rebuilt by a
script -- here `nexus_test`, and by the same logic the developer `nexus` -- which need it applied or their
tests will read a schema that no longer matches the code. That is the D79/"silence, not green" family
wearing a different hat: a compiled, wired endpoint whose table exists only in some databases is not
broken code, it is a partially-landed change, and only running the plane's own test says which it is.
This lane's `db_gate_fresh.sh` also keeps `schema_migrations` while the service keeps Flyway's
`flyway_schema_history` (the script's own D32 caveat), so a hand-built live database can be behind both
ledgers at once.

**Numbers.** One targeted migration apply, one module clean-compile (~30 s), two single-test runs; the
before/after is 5 run / 3 failed -> 5 run / 0 failed on
`com.nexus.growth.ShareLinkTest`. No source file changed, so nothing new is committed except this entry;
no other test class was run (the module's full `mvn -o test` still carries the untracked-package failures
#58 reports, which is why the single-class invocation was the attributable form).

**Limits.** (i) `nexus` -- the developer database -- was not checked; it may equally lack V7, and the
running :8090 service would fail the same three ways if asked. (ii) The `schema_migrations` bookkeeping for
that `--file` apply was not read back; the evidence is behavioural, not ledger-based. (iii) The three red
corners were the database-backed ones; two green tests in the same class were the argument that the
routing and validation layers were fine all along.

**next.** (a) Apply V7 to the developer database (or rebuild it) before anyone reads a :8090 share call as
a defect. (b) #34's open half is now "run in CI", not "wait for a lane". (c) Carried: #75's step-7 half,
#58, #73, #79, #44, #62, #64, #17, #19, step 11's residue, §87's seam, D91's served leg.

## D141 The developer database was never the gap -- and the test database has no migration ledger at all, which is a different finding than the one #93 expected — 2026-09-27

D140 left a suspicion with a number attached to it: if `nexus_test` had been quietly missing
`V7__share_links.sql`, the developer database `nexus` and the running :8090 service might be in the same
state, and the share write would be a demo that only passes in the places someone remembered to migrate.
This unit checks that, read-only, without touching a live database.

**Measurement (a): the developer plane is ahead, not behind.** In `nexus`, `to_regclass('public.share_links')`
is non-null among 61 tables, and `flyway_schema_history` ends at `version 7, success = t` with 6, 5, 4
below it. So the service's own migrator has already applied V7 -- the commit landed, the running
application's schema followed, and the D140 worry does not extend to this plane. Nothing was applied here;
there was nothing to apply.

**Measurement (b): the test plane has no ledger, so "did the --file apply record itself?" has no
answer.** `nexus_test` holds `share_links` (the count is 1), confirming D140's apply is still in place --
and `schema_migrations`, the table `db_apply_migrations.sh` keeps, does not exist in that database at all.
That refines the script's own D32 caveat rather than confirming it: the two ledgers it warns about
(Flyway's `flyway_schema_history`, the scripts' `schema_migrations`) are not both behind on `nexus_test`,
they are both absent. Whatever migrates that database -- surefire's own setup, or a person -- keeps no
ledger there, so the only evidence that a migration reached it is behavioural. That is exactly why the
D140 fix had to be proven by running the test rather than by reading a table, and it is the reason a
migration to `nexus_test` can silently drift: nothing there would notice.

**Not done, deliberately.** No call was made against :8090 -- the service is not running (`curl` to
`/actuator/health` returns no response), and starting another stream's developer service to satisfy my own
curiosity is a shared-environment action, not a verification I was owed. The schema question it would have
answered is answered by (a) instead, from the ledger the service itself maintains.

**Numbers.** Three read-only probes and one HTTP attempt; zero writes, zero DDL, zero service state
changed. `nexus`: table present, 61 tables, Flyway at 7/success. `nexus_test`: table present,
`schema_migrations` absent. :8090: down. #93 closes on that, with its live-call half left explicitly open.

**next.** (a) If a share call must be attested over HTTP, it needs the service up -- a decision for
whoever owns the dev environment, not a step to slip in. (b) The `nexus_test` no-ledger finding is worth
one line in the gate docs the next time this lane touches them: the only check that plane gets is the
tests that run against it. (c) Carried: #73, #75 (step-7 half), #58, #79, #44, #62, #64, #17, #19,
step 11's residue, §87's seam, D91's served leg.

## D142 The platform suite's 34 reds are one plane, not fourteen defects: `nexus_test` is running a schema from before V4 — 2026-09-27

D140 and D141 established that `nexus_test` keeps no migration ledger and that its only check is whatever
runs against it. This unit exercises that claim at scale, because the standing answer to "is the build
green?" had become a shrug: #58 carries "commerce/admin/seo test packages are untracked; red count
withdrawn", and the last honest baseline in the ledger was 206 run / 7 failures from the D50 era.

**Measurement.** `mvn -o -B test` in `services/platform`, 82 seconds: **Tests run: 217, Failures: 13,
Errors: 21**, BUILD FAILURE. The failing classes are mostly tracked, in-lane code --
`CollectionsReadTest` (13 errors), `CollectionDraftWriteTest` (5), `ModerationFlowTest`, three identity
door tests, `FactWriteTest`, `MerchantWorkspaceTest`, `RateLimitEnforcementTest` -- which is why counting
them as "other streams' untracked packages" is no longer a sufficient answer.

**The causes are two, and both are schema-plane, not code.** 18 distinct `duplicate key value violates
unique constraint` reports, 5 `there is no unique or exclusion constraint matching the ON CONFLICT
specification`, and the rest BadSqlGrammar: `insert into user_identities (user_id, tenant...)` and
`column ui.tenant_id does not exist`. Read together they say the database surefire runs against predates
`V4__tenant_scoped_identity.sql` (the migration that adds `user_identities.tenant_id`) and is also missing
unique constraints that later migrations added -- `users_email_uniq` firing on a test fixture's second
insert, and an `ON CONFLICT` target no longer present. The first failure of the run cascades: a test class
that cannot seed its rows reports a dozen errors in tenths of a millisecond each, which is what the 13-error
`CollectionsReadTest` block looks like.

**Why this lane did not fix it in place.** The honest repair is to rebuild `nexus_test` from
`infra/db/migrations/V*.sql` -- which is a destructive act on a database other streams' tests read, and
applying V4 forward by hand is worse: partial application against a schema that already diverged in both
directions produces exactly the silent drift D141 described. So the finding is filed and the decision is
put where it belongs, with the evidence to make it quickly. One data point in favour of the rebuild being
safe rather than merely possible: the 5 tests in the `com.nexus.growth` package and the whole
`SeoReadTest`/`UcpDoorsTest`/`platform.*` block pass against the same database, so nothing in the red set
looks like lost data; it looks like an old schema.

**Numbers.** One full suite run: 217 tests, 13 failures, 21 errors, 82 s; 9 failing classes named above;
18 duplicate-key + 5 ON-CONFLICT + 7 user_identities-grammar causes. Registry and gate state unchanged:
326 rows, 196 of 216 assertions witnessed, HEAD's step 5 green at 216 checks. No source file was edited by
this unit, and no database was modified.

**next.** (a) #94 asks whoever owns `nexus_test` to rebuild it from the migration set (or authorise this
lane to), then re-run `mvn -o test` for the first honest baseline since D50. (b) #58's "red count
withdrawn" should be replaced by that baseline rather than by an attribution to untracked packages, which
this run shows is only part of the story. (c) Carried: #73, #75 (step-7 half), #44, #79, #62, #64, #17,
#19, step 11's residue, §87's seam, D91's served leg.

### D142 amendment, measured the same day: `nexus_test` is not merely old, it is divergent in both directions — 2026-09-27

D142 concluded from the suite's own errors that `nexus_test` "runs a schema from before V4". A read-only
query now says that half-true, and the fuller shape matters for whoever acts on #94.

`nexus_test.user_identities` columns are `id, user_id, provider, provider_id, secret_ref, verified_at,
created_at` -- no `tenant_id`, where the developer database `nexus` has it: the V4 claim is confirmed.
But the same probe found `nexus_test` **does** hold `share_links` (D140's apply), holds 80
primary/unique constraints, and **has** an index named `users_email_uniq` -- while `nexus`, the database
that Flyway migrates, **does not** (`users_email_uniq` count 0; 61 tables there against 59 there). So the
two live databases are not "new and old"; each carries objects the other lacks, in opposite directions,
and the 18 duplicate-key errors are the sound of the *extra* constraint firing in a database whose columns
are also missing some.

That converts D141's warning from a prediction into an observation: a plane with no migration ledger
drifts both ways at once, and neither `db_gate_fresh.sh` (which builds a third schema from scratch and
passes) nor a single suite run can see it. #94's rebuild is therefore not a version bump but a
re-convergence: after it, the honest next step is to re-apply whatever `nexus_test` legitimately grew by
hand -- starting with V7, which that plane only ever received from this lane.

Nothing here changes the counts D142 reported (217 / 13 / 21 / 82 s), the classes named, or the
recommendation. It narrows its premise: the test database is not simply behind, it is different.

## D144 Repoint two comments at the section the renumber moved, and decline the two cheaper fixes for a red that is a superseded schema

A renumber is a local operation with a non-local blast radius: D115 brought the working copy'"'"'s stranded
sections back into `docs/STATUS.md` as §120-§123 (they had been §105-§108), and two Java comments that
had been written against the old numbers kept them. `scripts/check_status_citations.mjs` therefore exited 1
with exactly two offenders, which §148 had already written down as "its two known spelled-plane defects".
The section exists; only the pointer rotted.

**Three ways to make that checker green, and only one of them is honest.** Restore a `## 106.` heading so the
old pointer resolves again: that resurrects a number two ledgers and a recovery note now describe as
renumbered, and it gives every future reader two names for one section. Teach the checker to follow a
renumber history: now the checker carries a table that has to be maintained by hand, which is the same
class of debt §84 residue (e) owns for the directory exclusion list. Or repoint the two comments at the
section that actually holds the claim -- `STATUS §121`, "A required field no service serves, and the page
that threw on it", which is where "the web one threw `undefined.map` in live mode" moved. The third is two
edits, `CollectionsController.java:186` and `CollectionsReadTest.java:188`, and it is the only one where
the checker stays a checker. `§121` and not `§122`: §121 is the account of the crash; §122 is the account of
serving the field.

**The red that was left after that, and the fix this lane declined to make.** `mvn -o -B test` files 217 run
with 11 failures and 38 errors across 11 classes. 35 of the 38 errors are `DuplicateKeyException` on
`users_email_uniq`, and every one of the 11 failures is a downstream sound of the same thing -- a register
that answers 409 `email_taken`, a register that answers 500, a workspace list of size 0. Read-only probes
say why: `nexus_test.users` holds 1157 rows including `curator@example.test` and `writer@fav.test`, its
`users` indexes are `users_pkey, users_email_uniq, users_tenant_idx`, and it has no `schema_migrations`
table at all.

The cheap reading is "the fixtures reuse fixed addresses; make them unique". That reading is wrong, and the
evidence for it is in the migration that already fixed this. Every red class opens a new tenant first --
`newTenant` takes a random slug -- and then inserts the fixed address **into that new tenant**, which is
correct under `V4__tenant_scoped_identity.sql:44` (`users_email_tenant_uniq ON users(tenant_id, email)`)
and fatal under `V1__init.sql:46` (`users_email_uniq ON users(email)`), dropped at V4:43. A new tenant
cannot rescue a fixed address when the index does not look at the tenant. V4'"'"'s own header describes the
exact experiment -- "reproduced in the dev/test databases by simply running the demo login twice" -- and
`AuthService`'"'"'s "already registered in this tenant" is the V4 message being served by a V1 index. So the
tests are written for the shipped schema and the database is running the superseded one. Making the
addresses unique would turn this green while leaving a retired index in place, and the next divergence
would arrive the same way, without a red to announce it.

**Gates.** Measured on the final bytes of this text; §149 holds the full table. `db_gate_fresh.sh` 11/11
`RESULT: PASS`, 216 checks / 58 tables / 7 migrations; step 8 exit 0, step 9 PASS (73 comment citations,
21 files), step 10 PASS with §149 the one uncommitted section, step 11 PASS at 326 rows and 196 of 216
witnessed (90.7%); `check_status_citations.mjs` exit 0 at 8 of 8; contract drift 114/106 with 0 in every
drift category; jsonb exit 0; web `tsc --noEmit` clean and `vitest run` 128 passed; ai `pytest` 71 passed,
4 skipped. The one red is the suite above, reproduced as 217 / 11 / 38 with each of
`nexus-platform-postgres` and `nexus-platform-testpg` holding `127.0.0.1:5433` -- the two compose services
cannot run at once, and the number did not move with the container.

**Where that leaves #94.** Narrowed rather than started: bring `nexus_test` onto the migration set (V4 is
the load-bearing one), then re-apply what that plane legitimately grew by hand -- share_links, V7 -- as
