## D145 Wire the spelled §-citation checker into the gate, and rewrite the arm that had recorded the defect it was created for

§126 wrote the checker, proved it could fail (D117, six arms), and then shipped it unwired, with the reason
in its own words: its first run on the real tree was red at two offenders in another lane'"'"'s committed files,
and "a step nobody can make green teaches running the gate with the step skipped." That was the right call
then. The condition it named — #79'"'"'s two comments pointing at a `§106` that D115'"'"'s renumber had moved to
`§121` — closed in §149, so this unit does the second half: the checker becomes step 12, and eleven becomes
twelve.

**Why this step and not another.** Steps 8 and 9 resolve `File.java:NNN` against a file that exists and has
that many lines. A spelled `STATUS §NN` is a different claim — it resolves against a *heading*, and a heading
can be renumbered away while every file:line citation in the same sentence still resolves. That is not
hypothetical: it is exactly what happened to the two comments, and §148 recorded the resulting FAIL as a known
defect across four ledger sections before anyone fixed it, because nothing ran the reader. The gate now runs
it, and it reads HEAD — matching §126'"'"'s grammar ("must be a `## N. ` heading at HEAD") rather than the
working tree, which is the same choice step 10 makes for a different reason.

**Two things went wrong on the way and both are recorded rather than smoothed over.**

The step banner was written with backticks inside a double-quoted shell string — `` every `STATUS §NN` ... ``
— and bash performs command substitution on backticks inside double quotes. The first 12-step run therefore
printed `=== 12/12 ... — every  written outside a code span names a heading`, having executed `STATUS §NN` as
a command and printed nothing in its place. The step itself ran correctly; only its title was eaten. Dropping
the backticks is the fix, and it was found by reading the log, not by a check — a banner that prints nothing
is the same class of silent-empty that step 9'"'"'s "an empty scan is a FAIL" exists for, one plane over.

The falsifier reddened on a green tree. Arm 1 asserted the two offenders were BAD with `expect: 1`, and its
own comment said the arm "goes green only when the platform lane fixes them, which is #79 closing." §149
closed that half, so the arm reported `6 arms · 5 held · 1 missed` and `RESULT: FAIL` — a harness whose
control arm had encoded the defect as its expectation. The arm now asserts the positive form: an `ok` line
naming each file, line and the heading it points at, `expect: 0`. That holds while the fix holds, reddens if
either comment reverts to §106, and stops the harness from needing the tree to stay broken. It is the same
move D116 made one unit earlier when its own control arm reddened on its own writing, one plane along.

**What was not done, and why it is not covered by a green step 12.** #79 has two more halves: nine bare
`§106` comments in the identity lane, and four design-doc citations of which three sit on the frozen list.
Neither is read by this checker — it judges spelled `STATUS §NN` outside a code span and counts the rest as
mentions — so step 12 passing says nothing about them. §126 (d) also showed the obvious sweep would be wrong
in its second half: those nine want `TRACEABILITY §100`, not §121. Wiring a step that cannot see a residue is
not closing it, and the ledger says so instead of letting the green stand in for the rest.

**Gates, on the final bytes of this text** (§150 carries the census): `db_gate_fresh.sh` 12/12 `gate_rc=0`,
`RESULT: PASS — 216 quality checks on a from-scratch schema (tables=58, migrations=7)`; step 12 PASS at 10 of
10 spelled citations; `falsify_status_citations.mjs` 6 arms, 6 held, exit 0; `check_falsifier_registry.mjs`
PASS at 326 rows and 196 of 216 witnessed (90.7%); `check_ledger_citations.mjs --worktree` exit 0 with 0
offenders; `check_comment_citations.mjs` PASS at 73 across 21 files; `check_ledger_sections.mjs` PASS with
§149-§150 and D144-D145 the only uncommitted headings; `check_contract_drift.mjs` 114/106 and 0 in every
drift category; `check_jsonb_reads.mjs` exit 0; web `tsc --noEmit` clean and `vitest run` 128 passed; ai
`pytest` 71 passed, 4 skipped. `mvn -o -B test` remains 217 / 11 failures / 38 errors — this unit touched two
comments and a shell script, and the suite'"'"'s red is #94'"'"'s schema divergence, measured in §149 (b)-(c).

## D146 The third mutation plane: arms that change the schema, because fifteen of the last twenty unwitnessed rows are about the schema

#73 closed its data era at 196 of 216. D128 had already sorted the remaining twenty by *what kind of
mutation can reach them*, and D129 spent the nine that a row-write could reach, which left the count sitting
on a claim this lane had never tested: that the other eleven are unreachable not because nobody looked hard
enough but because the state they forbid is one the **schema** blocks. Every arm in
`data/seed/falsifier_plants.py` up to now moves a row. D122's arms move a row the database refuses and say
so (they open with `SET LOCAL session_replication_role = replica`, which reaches the referential state and
nothing else); D126's arms move a row the database accepts. Neither family can produce a priced offering
whose `price_updated_at` is NULL, because that column is `NOT NULL` — the door is the schema's own, and a
census row about a door cannot be falsified from the side of the data.

**The mechanism, and what it does not claim.** Postgres DDL is transactional, so the seventh family needs no
new harness: `BEGIN; ALTER TABLE ...; <the whole shipped gate body>; ROLLBACK` puts the mutated schema in
front of the same 216 assertions in the same session, and the rollback un-does the DDL exactly as it un-does
a row. The closing baseline still has to come back identical, which is how the drive knows it left the
database as it found it; the connection is the superuser, because the plant is a schema change and no
application role can or should make one. What such an arm proves is *narrower* than what a data plant
proves, and the arm labels say so in the same way D122's say it: a schema-plane plant witnesses that the
assertion **detects** a state, never that a door could produce one. The route in is a migration — a `V9` that
drops a `NOT NULL`, a table created beside a waiver that called it absent — which is precisely the seam
these rows exist to watch.

**Seven arms, and what each one moved.** Each arm is one whole run of the shipped gate body against a mutated schema, inside a transaction the
session rolls back. The tables below are the drive's own columns: rows the gate filed, whether the named
target reddened, collateral reds, and names that stopped being filed (every one of them 216 / 0, which is
what makes a schema plant safe to replay against a shared database).

  arm                                                     rows  target  coll.  unfiled
  CREATE TABLE agents                            -> no-referent waiver    RED    0      0
  CHECK 4 labels -> 3                            -> CHECK/door agreement  RED    0      0
  DROP COLUMN share_links.subject_type           -> door vocab exists     RED    1      0
  ADD COLUMN merchants.address_verified          -> boolean evidence      RED    0      0
  ADD COLUMN documents.doc_lang varchar(32)      -> string census types   RED    1      0
  DROP NOT NULL price_updated_at + NULL one row  -> priced provenance     RED    1      0
  insert+dangle share_links.created_by / .tenant_id -> the two fk: names  RED    3      0  (each)

All seven then ran again as part of the whole 155-arm drive: `RESULT: PASS`, 158 whole-gate sessions,
closing baseline 216 assertions / red = 0, identical to the opening one. 17 registry rows appended (8 from
an arm's own RED, 9 from collateral), and step 11 re-read the record at 343 rows and 204 of 216 assertions
witnessed — 94.4%, up from the 196 (90.7%) every entry on this arc had been quoting.


**One prediction that failed loudly, which is the right way to fail.** The narrowed-CHECK arm was written
against a constraint name transcribed from the naming convention (`share_links_subject_type_check`) rather
than from the plane; the real name, which this lane had queried and printed earlier in the same sitting, is
`share_links_subject_type_known`. The session did not go green and did not report a MISS — it reported
`run ABORTED rc=3: ERROR: constraint ... does not exist` and the drive exited 1. That is the shape a
mistyped plant should have: a plant that names nothing cannot reach anything, and a harness that treated an
unreadable run as a green arm would turn a transcription error into a witnessed assertion. The name was
repointed at what `pg_constraint` says and the arm then reddened its target with zero collateral.

**Two stale claims retired on the way in.** `KNOWN_RED` held the two rows D108 declared red because
`share_links` existed only on an uncommitted migration; `d7c2d57` committed V7 and §149 measured the gate
building it (migrations=7, tables=58), so the baseline is 216 assertions and 0 red, and an empty `KNOWN_RED`
is the honest state. A declaration that no longer describes the plane is worse than no declaration at all:
it would let either of those two rows come back genuinely red and be filed as the other lane's. The same
reason retires the D125 list comment's "minus share_links' two, which exist only on an uncommitted
migration" — those two names are on the plane, the child table is empty, so they are exactly D125's
insert-then-dangle case, and both arms landed with the three collateral rows that mechanism always drags
(`no traffic outside the seeded tables`, `every reference the seed writes is probed or explained`,
`every column that cannot vary`) because the synthetic row is written outside the 23-table anchor.

**What the eight new witnesses do not buy.** The eight new witnesses are the eighth, ninth and tenth of the twenty sorted by D128, not the eleven
that remain. Two of the twelve left are now known to be vacuous-by-empty-census rather than untested
(`a join-one-type waiver is only true while the table ships one type` reads a registry that carries zero
rows of that kind, so the only plant that reddens it edits `quality.sql`'s own hand lists); and the
strongest claim this unit can make about the rest is a *prediction* it did not spend: three of them
(`an armed type resolves in a table the schema has`, `the pairs declared probed are pairs the schema has`,
`the registry names no column the schema has lost`) sit behind static `WITH probe AS (...)` UNIONs that
read the very columns a plant would have to remove, so the whole-gate replay is expected to error out
before the report — which the drive would then report as `run ABORTED rc=3` rather than as a green arm.
An abort measured is a disposition; an untested claim is not, and that measurement is the next unit.

**Gates, on the final bytes of this text** (§151 carries the census): `check_ledger_citations.mjs --worktree` exit 0 at 277 headings / 568 name:number tokens / 344 citation-shaped / 0 offenders; `check_comment_citations.mjs` PASS at 73 citations across 21 files (28 distinct files cited) — this unit touched no source comment; `check_ledger_sections.mjs` PASS with STATUS 118 at HEAD / 119 on disk and DECISIONS 132 / 133, D146 and §151 the only disk-only headings, 0 missing and 0 numbers claimed twice; `check_status_citations.mjs` PASS, every spelled `STATUS §NN` resolving to a heading at HEAD; `check_falsifier_registry.mjs --db nexus_gate_283340_1790454442` PASS at 343 rows, 204 of 216 witnessed (94.4%), 304 commit and 39 file witnesses.
                    
                    `db_gate_fresh.sh` was not re-run, because no gate file, reader or migration changed; the shipped code touched is the plant harness, and its 158 whole-gate sessions are the gate body sliced out of `quality.sql` executed against a mutated schema inside a transaction that is rolled back — the identical closing baseline is what certifies that. `mvn -o -B test` stays 217 / 11 failures / 38 errors, which is #94's divergent `nexus_test`, unchanged by a harness-only unit.

## D147 The schema plane reaches the last three plantable rows, and the first of them turns out to watch a key the project never writes — 2026-09-27

**Why this unit.** D146 opened the schema plane and left twelve named rows. `STATUS §151`'s next (a) spent three of
them by mechanism — *a jsonb element, a trailing view column and a citext cast* — and next (b) said the three
candidates behind static `WITH probe AS (...)` UNIONs have to be *measured* rather than written off. Both ran.
204 becomes 207 of 216 (95.8%), the registry goes 343 -> 348 rows, and the plantable queue is now empty: every one
of the nine that remain sits in a group with a stated reason, and three of those nine have an error message behind
the reason instead of a prediction.

**Three arms, three single-arm drives, one loaded database.** Each drive is its own `BEGIN; plant; whole gate
body; report; ROLLBACK` session set against `nexus_gate_283340_1790454442`, and each printed the same shape:
baseline 216 assertions and 0 red, target RED, 0 assertions unfiled, closing baseline identical.

| arm | plane | target | collateral | rows |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| a real guide item gains a `merchant_id` pointing at nothing | data (jsonb element) | `collections/guides reference live merchants` | `the elements of an object-array column all carry the same keys` | 216 |
| `users.email` cast from citext to text | schema | `a census that folds case reports both readings and which one the demo exercises` | `the string census declares a reading for every type it catches` | 216 |
| `v_merchant_funnel` gains a trailing column no answer block explains | schema | `a served view answers every column it exposes` | none | 216 |

Three drives to validate, three re-run with `--emit-rows` (arm commit `dc3ac65`, row commit `e9ec80b`), each at
rc=0: 2 + 2 + 1 rows appended, three of them the first witness an assertion of that name ever carried. `--only`
was used deliberately: a single-arm drive costs three whole-gate sessions, and the fleet is 158 arms.

**The finding, which is the reason this unit is not just three rows.** The first arm was aimed by D132's note and
then measured, and the measurement says the row is aimed at the wrong key. Two planes agree: on the gate database
and on `nexus`, 4 collections carry items, **0** of those element objects carry a `merchant_id` key, and all 38
elements carry `subject_id` with `subject_type = 'merchant'` (19 `collection`, 10 `guide`, 9 `itinerary`). The seed
therefore never writes the key the row reads. The read path does not either: `CollectionsController.merchantIdOf()`
resolves `subject_type` then `subject_id` and never looks at `merchant_id`, and `CollectionsWriteController.
requireItems()` copies every key as written while validating only that a cited `subject_id` is a uuid — existence is
explicitly the read's job, reported on `dropped_item_ids`. So the state the row is *named for* is reachable by a
door, and the row does not see it. Measured, not argued: a scratch probe (not an arm) repointed all four
collections' first merchant-typed element at a ghost uuid — a payload the door accepts by design — and **0 of the
216 assertions moved**, while the same transaction confirms `dangling=4`. The plant that does redden the row works
because it introduces a key the project does not use, which is exactly why its registry label says so out loud.
This is a report for `data/seed/quality.sql`'s owner, not an edit: re-aiming the row at
`subject_type = 'merchant'` + `subject_id` would make it read the 38 references that exist and would catch what the
probe could not.

**The three candidates written off, with the abort that writes them off.** D146 predicted these would error out of
the whole-gate replay; the drive was run to collect the text instead of assuming it. `ALTER TABLE permission_grants
DROP COLUMN subject_id` aborts with `column "subject_id" does not exist` inside `WITH g AS (SELECT subject_type,
subject_id::text sid, ...)`, and `DROP TABLE api_keys` aborts with `relation "api_keys" does not exist` inside the
same probe's own `UNION ALL SELECT 'api_key', id::text, NULL FROM api_keys`. That disposes of
`an armed type resolves in a table the schema has`, `the pairs declared probed are pairs the schema has` and
`the registry names no column the schema has lost`: the objects they watch are the objects the report is computed
FROM, so no rolled-back DDL plant can witness them from a whole-gate replay. Reaching them means splicing a single
assertion, which is the plane D65 gave up on deliberately — a spliced row answers "did this predicate move" and
hides every collateral, and a harness that hides collateral cannot tell a good plant from a broken fixture.

**Two claims this unit retires.** (i) D132 grouped `a census that folds case reports both readings…` under *three
rows that are true because the schema or the seed forbids the state they watch for*, and said its red "needs two
citext values differing only by case". It does not: the row went red when the citext **type left the census**,
which is the direction that matters — a declared reading for a type no column any longer has. (ii) That same group
of three is now closed outright, because all of `price_updated_at present for priced offerings` (D146 dropped its
NOT NULL), `a census that folds case…` and `collections/guides reference live merchants` have witnesses. A write-off
that a later plane overtakes has to be corrected in the ledger, not left standing as a superseded fact.

**What the three new witnesses do not buy.** The collections row's witness shows the *predicate* detects a dangling
`merchant_id`; it buys nothing about the 38 references that exist, and the probe above shows the gate is blind to
those. The citext arm shows the fold row and the string-census reading row both detect a type leaving the schema —
it does not show the demo exercises case folding, which is the second half of that row's name. The view arm shows
the answered-column census notices an unexplained column; it says nothing about whether the view is correct. And all
three are schema/data-plane plants inside a transaction: they witness detection by the assertion, never that a door
could produce the state — D122's distinction, unchanged.

**The nine the reader still names.** `a join-one-type waiver is only true while the table ships one type`,
`a probe arm is a declared type and every armed type has an arm`, `the arm registry agrees with the probed-pair
counts`, `the polymorphic-pair census reads the catalogue`, `the reference census reads the catalogue` and
`traffic sweep reaches the whole closure, not a hand list` have both sides written inside `quality.sql` or count a
whole-schema floor, so a data/schema plant cannot reach them without editing the file under test — D132's nine,
minus the served-view row this unit landed. The other three are the aborts above. Nothing here is a "no more ideas"
list: the six file-plane rows say what a *fourth* mechanism would have to be (plant the sliced gate body's own text
in memory, never the tracked file), and that is a decision, not a leftover.

**Gates.** `check_falsifier_registry.mjs --db nexus_gate_283340_1790454442` PASS at 348 rows, 207 of 216 witnessed
(95.8%), 309 commit and 39 file witnesses, 9 gaps named. No gate file, reader or migration changed, so
`db_gate_fresh.sh` was not re-run; the shipped code touched is the plant harness and its eighteen whole-gate sessions
are the evidence. `mvn -o -B test` is untouched by a harness-only unit and stays at #94's 217 / 11 failures / 38
errors on the divergent `nexus_test`.

## D148 The fourth mutation plane is text: seven plants rewrite the sliced gate body in memory, and the falsifier registry closes at 216 of 216 — 2026-09-28

**Why this unit.** `STATUS §152`'s next (b) put the choice in writing: close #73's residue by decision — six
file-plane rows as a named, reasoned write-off — or build the mechanism the same section had named. The mechanism
was built. Seven arms now rewrite the gate body this drive slices, in memory, and the fleet goes from 158 arms to
165. `check_falsifier_registry.mjs` reports **216 of 216 (100.0%)** with an empty gap list where §152 left nine
names, and the registry is 348 -> 359 rows.

**What a text plant is.** A data plant changes rows, a schema plant changes DDL, and both leave the report's own
SQL alone. A text plant changes the sentence: `apply_edits(body, edits)` takes the string `gate_body()` already
sliced out of `data/seed/quality.sql`, applies `(anchor, replacement)` pairs to it in this process, and hands the
result to `gate_under()`, which runs it in a `BEGIN … ROLLBACK` session exactly as the other three planes do. The
tracked file is never written and the database is never touched outside the transaction, so the shipped artifact
and the gate's own plane are the same bytes before and after. Three things make the aim auditable rather than
convenient: the anchor has to occur **exactly once** in the shipped body or the drive raises before a session
opens (a plant that silently aimed at a phrase's second occurrence would report a red the real file never
contained); the judgment printed for the run is the same `target RED / collateral / unfiled` table a data arm is
judged by; and the arm's name says which plane it ran on, so a reader of `falsifiers.tsv` cannot mistake a text
witness for a data one.

**The seven arms, and the row each one moves.**

| target assertion | what the plant rewrites in the sliced body | own | collateral |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `an armed type resolves in a table the schema has` | the hand vocabulary `poly_vocab` gains an `arm` row whose referent table does not exist | RED | `a probe arm is a declared type and every armed type has an arm` |
| `the pairs declared probed are pairs the schema has` | the probe list `poly_probed` gains a probe over `plant_ghost_table` | RED | `every probe family resolves at least one armed type`, `the arm registry agrees with the probed-pair counts` |
| `a join-one-type waiver is only true while the table ships one type` | a registered column is re-classified `kind = 'join-one-type'`, its name chosen by `SELECT … FROM ref_cat WHERE types_n > 1 …`, not transcribed | RED | none |
| `the registry names no column the schema has lost` | `ref_registry` gains `plant.ghost_column` | RED | none |
| `the reference census reads the catalogue` | the census's own enumeration is narrowed to tables carrying a `subject_type` column — the census mistaking itself for the polymorphic probe | RED | `the registry names no column the schema has lost` |
| `the polymorphic-pair census reads the catalogue` | the pair census is narrowed to the four tables the hand list already names | RED | none |
| `traffic sweep reaches the whole closure, not a hand list` | the recursive closure walk's `fk.contype = 'f'` becomes `'x'`, so the walk stops following any edge | RED | `no traffic outside the seeded tables` |

**Aimed by measurement before any session was spent.** The two census plants and the traffic plant each had to
land on the correct side of a published floor, and floors are the one place an off-by-one turns a designed red
into a coincidence. So the shipped predicates were read out-of-process first: `ref_cat` enumerates **26** columns
over both naming shapes, and narrowing it to tables that carry a `subject_type` column leaves **14** against a
floor of `>= 17`; `poly_cat` enumerates **12** (type, id) pairs, and restricting it to the four tables
`poly_probed` names leaves **4** against a floor of `>= 8`; the traffic sweep counts **29** in its closure walk
against a floor of `>= 20`. Two of the three fall below their floor with margin, so a green would have been a
real surprise. The traffic arm does not need to cross its floor — it removes edges from a closure the row claims
is complete, and the row's own `no traffic outside the seeded tables` sibling moved with it, which is the
collateral the harness exists to make visible.

**The arm that went green first, and what that green measured.** The join-one-type arm's first design inserted a
registry row for a column the census reports as multi-type but the registry had not listed. Through the real
harness it produced a **green**, and the drive failed as designed: `RESULT: FAIL -- … the assertion naming it
stayed green`, rc=1. That green is a finding, not a fluke: read the plane, and every column the census reports
with `types_n > 1` is already registered, so the row is held by *exhaustion* — there is no unregistered
multi-type column left for a plant to name. Re-aimed at a re-classification instead of an addition (change a
real registered column's `kind` to a waiver its own table's data refutes), it reddened with zero collateral. Two
lessons recorded rather than absorbed: an arm aimed at a row guarded by exhaustion has to attack the row's
*meaning*, not its coverage; and a drive that refuses to emit rows unless every arm reddened is what turned a
would-be silent false witness into a measurement.

**Two anchors caught out of process.** Before the first session, a scratch probe re-ran the anchor rule against
the shipped file: two entries carried `edits` as a flat `[anchor, replacement]` instead of `[(anchor,
replacement)]`, and one anchor had been typed with its trailing period dropped, so it occurred 0 times. All three
were fixed at zero session cost. The rule earns its place by that: the failure mode of a text plant is aiming at
the wrong sentence, and the file — not the database — is the thing under test.

**A claim this unit retires.** D147 wrote that reaching the three aborted rows "means splicing a single
assertion, which is the plane D65 gave up on deliberately — a spliced row answers 'did this predicate move' and
hides every collateral". It does not. Those runs aborted because a *schema* plant removed an object the report is
computed FROM, so the session died before the report existed. A text plant removes the sentence, not the object:
the whole gate body still runs, every one of the 216 assertions is still counted, and the collateral column is
still full: four of the seven arms printed collateral rows, eleven rows came out of the drive, and step 11 still
names no gap. Nothing was spliced in this unit, which also retires D132's standing
objection that these rows are unreachable because "a plant would have to edit the file under test, and a green
there proves the file agrees with itself": the objection is about a green, and every arm here produced a red
against an unmutated baseline that stayed 216 / 0.

**What 216 of 216 does not buy — stated before the number is quoted anywhere else.**
(i) A text witness is narrower in kind than a data witness. It shows *this comparison is live: it moves when one
side drifts*. It never shows the shipped seed is wrong — the shipped seed's claim rests entirely on the
unmutated 216 / 0 baseline, which no text arm touches and which this drive printed at both ends.
(ii) The percentage is now saturated, which means it has stopped being the interesting question. §152 proved a
row can carry a witness and still read a key nothing in the project writes:
`collections/guides reference live merchants` reddens under a plant that adds a `merchant_id` element key the
demo ships **0** of, while a ghost `subject_id` — the key all 38 real references use — moves 0 of 216. That row
is witnessed today, at 100.0%, and still blind. 100% witnessed means every assertion has *a* state that would
make it answer differently; it does not mean every assertion reads the column the product writes. #95 stays open
for exactly that reason, and closing the registry must not be read as closing it.
(iii) Detection is not reachability. None of the seven shows a door can produce the state — D122's distinction,
unchanged by a fourth plane.

**Gates.** `check_falsifier_registry.mjs --db nexus_gate_283340_1790454442 --container nexus-platform-postgres`
PASS: 359 rows, 216 of 216 (100.0%), 320 commit / 39 file witnesses, no gap named. One seven-arm drive
(`--only "text plane:"`, which selects exactly the seven), 9 whole-gate sessions, opening and closing baseline
both 216 assertions / red = 0 and identical, arm commit `c5ba5af` and row commit `e228c56`. `db_gate_fresh.sh`
was not re-run for the drive: no gate file, reader, migration or product source changed, and the only shipped
artifact step 11 reads — this harness and the registry — was re-read on the final bytes. The citation steps were
re-run after this entry and `STATUS §153` landed, because a ledger append is where the spelled-§ reader has
before now caught every new red.
## D149 A vacuity census that refuted its own draft finding: the gate already measures every element key the build reads — what it never asks is whether a predicate's key is one of them — 2026-09-28

**Why this unit.** `STATUS §153`'s next (a) named the question that the saturated witness percentage cannot answer:
not *can this row be reddened* but *does this row read a key the product writes*. #95 was one such case found by
accident; this unit went looking for the rest with a census, and the census turned against its own hypothesis.

**What was measured.** First the plane: the whole twelve-step fresh gate re-run on the post-D148 tree —
`RESULT: PASS — 216 quality checks on a from-scratch schema (tables=58, migrations=7)`, rc=0, gate database kept
as `nexus_gate_369684_1790536129`, and step 11 green there with the 359-row registry (the first full-gate
measurement *after* the text plane landed, which is the run that shows the new arms cost the shipped gate nothing).
Then presence: every jsonb key that appears in a `quality.sql` read was counted on two planes (`nexus` and the
kept gate database) — rows carrying the key out of rows in the container, and, for array-topped columns, elements
carrying it out of elements. The `nexus` numbers: `merchants.contact.phone` 520/520, `offerings.attributes.data_origin`
5534/5534, `facts.value.value` 1727/5688, `facts.value.estimated` 1560/5688, and five keys resolving to nothing —
`offerings.attributes ? 'import_job'` 0 of 5,534, `collections.seo ? 'generated_by'` 0 of 4,
`collections.items[] ? 'merchant_id'` 0 of 38 elements (all 38 carry `subject_id`), `agent_runs.plan ? 'steps'`
0 of 4, `events.properties ? 'query'` 0 of 4.

**The draft finding, and the file that killed it.** Those last two looked like a mechanism gap: the read census's
own predicate is `format('%I ? %L', col, key)` over a *column*, and on an array-topped column that returns false
for every key no matter what the elements hold — measured directly, `collections.items ? 'subject_id'` is 0 of 4
rows while 38 of 38 elements carry it, and `merchants.images ? 'url'` is 0 of 520 rows while 520 of 520 elements
carry it. From there the hypothesis was that element keys sit outside the census plane altogether. `quality.sql`
says otherwise, two sections later: `$d81b$` (quality.sql:1885-1920) walks every jsonb column, keeps the ones with
array-topped rows (`CONTINUE WHEN w = 0`), and files rows, array-topped rows, element count, distinct element
signatures and — decisively — **the union of the element keys** into `arr_cat`; `arr_bound` answers each such
column by name (quality.sql:1939 files `('collections','items','payload-shape','-', '38 objects across 4
collections, one signature')`), and assertions at quality.sql:1945-1969 count and cross-check that census. D81
built this in the same file whose row #95 is about. The hypothesis is withdrawn, and the withdraw is the entry's
point: a census built from a hand grep over `->>'key'` had already been told in this project's own ledger that the
grep is the wrong instrument, and it was the shipped `arr_cat` walk, not my regex, that settled it.

**What survives, narrower and sharper.** Re-derive #95 against the plane that now exists. The element key union
is measured, and on `nexus` it reads `collections.items → note, subject_id, subject_type` and
`merchants.images → alt, credit, url`. So the gate *knows* `merchant_id` is not a key of any `items` element —
and the row at quality.sql:1003 still asks `it->>'merchant_id' IS NOT NULL AND NOT EXISTS (…)`, which is false by
construction over that vocabulary. The missing piece is not a census but a join: **no assertion anywhere asks
whether a key that a *predicate* reads is one of the keys the same column's elements actually carry.** The two
planes hold the answer and are never compared, which is exactly why a row can be witnessed red (D147), be counted
by an element census (D81), and still read a key nothing writes. That is a report for the seed lane, not an edit,
and it is a cheap one: one row joining the predicate-named keys to `arr_cat.keys`, and the D148 text plane can
then witness it the way it witnessed the other seven, since its both-sides-live-in-the-file shape is precisely
what that plane was built for.

**Two shipped classifications independently confirmed, and a grammar lesson.** The two `dead-reader` rows in
`read_answer` are right as measured: `import_job` 0 of 5,534 and `generated_by` 0 of 4, matching the reason each
row states. And of the 15 keys my grep collected, 3 (`steps`, `query`, and one `key`) were never reads at all —
they are prose inside `--` comment lines (quality.sql:2482, :2498, :2509, :2519, :2558, :3425, :3434, :3435), two
of which *already record* that the read they mention resolves to nothing. A census that does not exclude the
comment plane invents reads; the shipped readers (`scripts/check_jsonb_reads.mjs`, which parses the answer tables,
and `$d81b$`, which parses the catalogue) do, and a hand grep does not.

**What this unit does not buy.** No shipped artifact changed, so no gate number moved: 216 assertions and 359
registry rows before and after. The measurement is read-only over two planes, and the presence counts are a
property of those planes — `nexus` carries 4 `agent_runs` where the comment at quality.sql:3434 reports 40, so a
count quoted from one is not a count of the other. Nothing here shows the guide-merchant row is *wrong* about
merchants: it shows the row cannot be right about the shipped payloads, which is the weaker and provable claim.

**Gates.** `scripts/db_gate_fresh.sh --keep` full twelve steps PASS (above). The four ledger readers were re-run
after this entry and `STATUS §154` landed: step 8 (`--worktree`), step 9 (73 comment-plane citations across 21
files), step 10 (`HEAD 122 sections · on disk 122 · missing 0 · duplicate 0`), step 12 — all rc=0.

## D150 The text plane's anchor rule had never been asked to refuse: `--self-test` witnesses the guard, and gate step 11 arms it — 2026-09-28

**Why this unit.** D148 gave the harness a rule — an anchor must match exactly one sentence of the sliced gate
body — and stated that a plant aiming at a phrase's second occurrence "would report a red the shipped text never
contained". Nothing in the repository had ever made that rule refuse anything, and this project has a written
standard for that shape of artifact: D103's record was only worth anything once step 11 executed the checker,
because "a record validated only when someone remembers to pass `--db` is a claim with a script next to it". A
guard that has never refused is the same claim in code.

**What landed.** `self_test()` in `data/seed/falsifier_plants.py` and a `--self-test` flag that runs it and
exits: no database, no container, no psql session, seconds instead of a drive. It does three things — re-applies
every shipped arm's edits against the body as it is on disk now (which is also a drift check: an anchor broken
by a later seed edit is named before anyone pays nine whole-gate sessions to find out), refuses an anchor the
body cannot contain, and refuses anchors the body genuinely repeats. The refusals are built from phrases the
sliced file really does carry rather than from an invented string, so the probe cannot pass because its own
fixture is easy. Then `scripts/db_gate_fresh.sh` step 11 runs it immediately before the registry reader, so an
anchor that stops being aimable reddens the gate.

**Measured.** Against the shipped body (250,701 chars, 3,593 lines): all **7** arm anchor sets accepted, each
matching exactly once; **five** refusals, each printing its own count — `0x` for a table name the file never had,
and `115x` (`INSERT INTO qc`), `10x` (`ORDER BY 1, 2`), `13x` (`jsonb_typeof(`), `231x`
(`SELECT count(*) FROM`). Self-test rc=0.

**The mutation control.** Weakening the guard in a scratch copy — `if n != 1:` → `if False:`, the tracked file
untouched — makes `self_test()` return 1 naming five acceptances, including
`a 0-occurrence anchor was accepted` and `a 115-occurrence anchor ('INSERT INTO qc') was accepted`; the unmutated
control in the same process returns 0. One mutant, caught 1/1. And the consequence the guard actually prevents was
measured separately, with the permissive version standing in for the shipped one: the same doubly-true anchor
lands its plant at **line 161** — one of 115 sites — while the other 114 look identical to the one the arm names.
The drive's table would print an ordinary red about an ordinary row, and the sentence it rewrote would be a
different sentence. That is why this guard is behavioral rather than cosmetic, and why the check is "raises"
rather than "the body changed".

**What this does not buy.** It witnesses the *anchor rule*, not any assertion: the 216 / 216 registry (§153) is
what shows rows can redden, and a self-test that merely ran the arms' `apply_edits` would prove only that. It also
cannot catch an anchor that matches exactly once but in the wrong sentence — unique-and-misaimed is invisible to
counting, and is caught only by the arm's own predicted red, which is why `--emit-rows` still refuses to write a
single row from a drive where any arm failed. And `--db` becoming optional is a CLI relaxation with a measured
backstop: a drive with no `--db` exits 1 with `FATAL: a drive needs --db (or run --self-test…)`.

**Gates.** The full twelve-step `scripts/db_gate_fresh.sh` was re-run after this wiring: `gate rc=0`, 216 checks on
a from-scratch schema (tables=58, migrations=7), and step 11's block prints the self-test ahead of the registry
reader — 7 accepted, five refusals — before that reader opens its first session. `STATUS §155` quotes that log.

**What the PASS does not prove, stated before anyone reads it as proof.** A run in which the guard passes cannot
distinguish "the guard is armed" from "the guard's return code is thrown away". The call is piped
(`… --self-test ) 2>&1 | sed`), and a pipe is where an exit code goes to die unless `pipefail` holds it. The
script does set `-euo pipefail` at its line 30, but reading a `set` line is not a measurement of it: the claim
"step 11 can stop the gate" is only witnessed by a run in which the guard returns 1 and the gate dies there,
never reaching step 12. That run is the next unit, and until it exists this entry's wiring claim is a shell-
semantics argument, not a red.

## D151 Step 11's guard is armed, not merely printed: a tracked `PYTHON` shim makes the gate die at step 11 and the death is attributable to the guard alone — 2026-09-28

**Why this unit.** D150 wired `--self-test` into `scripts/db_gate_fresh.sh` step 11 and STATUS §155 recorded two
full runs of that plane, both `RESULT: PASS`. Its own text named what those runs cannot show: the call is piped
into `sed`, and a pipe is where an exit code goes to die unless `pipefail` holds it. The script does set
`-euo pipefail` at line 30 — but a run in which the guard passes is equally consistent with "the guard's return
code is thrown away", and reading a `set` line is an argument about shell semantics rather than a measurement of
this gate. §155 left the claim unproven on purpose. This unit pays it.

**What landed.** `scripts/falsify_gate_selftest.sh`, joining the repository's existing falsifier family
(`falsify_ledger_sections.mjs`, `falsify_status_citations.mjs`). It returns 1 when and only when one of its
arguments is `--self-test`, and otherwise `exec python "$@"`, so the interpreter every other step uses is the
real one. It is invoked the way the gate already invites invocation — through the `PYTHON` knob at
`db_gate_fresh.sh:153` and `:330` — which means no tracked file is edited to arm the mutation, the shape D98's
`LEDGER_SECTIONS_DIR` and D101's `--plane` established.

**Measured, against predictions written before the log was read** (`D151.predictions.md`). Two probes, so the
tracked file is the one that stops the gate and not only a Temp copy of it:

  - probe A (Temp copy of the shim): log 132 lines. `=== 11/12` present, then the shim's own line
    `text-plane self-test, MUTATED: the guard returns 1 without looking at the body`, then nothing.
    `grep -c "gate assertions   216\|=== 12/12"` = **0** — the registry reader never started and step 12 never
    ran. `gate rc=1`, the predicted value. Gate databases before and after: **4**, so the EXIT trap at line 101
    still dropped the run's own database on a failed step.
  - probe B (tracked `scripts/falsify_gate_selftest.sh` via `PYTHON=$PWD/…`): all six predictions hold again, and
    the two logs are the same run twice — normalising only the generated database name, they differ in **2 lines**,
    both seed-window timestamps at step 4 (`03:32:47` vs `03:38:03`). Step headers present: 1/12 through 11/12,
    no 12/12.
  - the shim's two behaviors, checked on the tracked file in seconds before either gate run: as `PYTHON` for a
    real call it passes through (`print(1)` → `1`, rc=0); for `--self-test` it prints MUTATED and exits 1.

**The control is a green run of the same gate, read the same session.** The two runs recorded in §155 —
`RESULT: PASS — 216 quality checks on a from-scratch schema (tables=58, migrations=7)` and `gate rc=0` — share
the shim's steps 1-10 line for line: comparing the probe's 14 step and RESULT lines against the control's, with
the run's own database name normalised, gives **0 differing lines**. So the death at step 11 is not a seed step
breaking, not another lane's tree moving, and not the shim leaking into `generate.py`.

**What this does not buy.** It witnesses one step's entry point. The same question for steps 8 and 9 is still
open and has a measured shape: `check_ledger_citations.mjs:110` accepts `--text=<path>` and its own comment says
that flag exists so "a witness must be able to show an arm failing without writing a tracked file that two other
lanes are appending to", and `check_comment_citations.mjs:44` accepts `--plane <dir>` — yet the gate then called them
with hardcoded arguments at `db_gate_fresh.sh:207` and `db_gate_fresh.sh:218` then, so the capability is in the checker and unreachable from the gate.
Both arms were pre-flight-verified standalone in seconds before any long run was spent on them: a Temp ledger
citing line 99999 of `CollectionsController.java` exits 1 and names the file's real 453 lines, and a Temp plane holding
the same fake citation in a comment exits 1 likewise. Along the way the `--text` path refused two invalid
fixtures before it accepted one — no `## ` heading, then "1 citation(s) found and 0 file(s) resolved" — which is
the checker's own vacuity guard working, not a defect.

**And a census fact about the falsifier family itself.** `grep -rn falsify` over `.github/workflows/`,
`Makefile`, `scripts/*.sh`, `scripts/*.mjs` and `data/seed/*.py` returns eleven lines, every one of them a
comment, a usage string or prose — including this file's own header. No gate step and no CI job executes any
falsifier script. They are run by hand and quoted in the ledgers. D103's sentence about a
record applies to them exactly — a witness validated only when someone remembers to run it is a claim with a
script next to it — and the difference between this family and step 11's guard is that the guard now also runs
unbidden, inside the gate. Whether the family should be wired the same way is the next question, not this one's
answer.

**Gates.** The two §155 runs (216 checks, `gate rc=0`) are the baseline and the two probes above are the
mutation. Because D150 appended to both ledgers, the two hand-run falsifiers that read those ledgers were re-run
rather than assumed intact: `falsify_status_citations.mjs` **6 arms · 6 held · 0 missed**, exit 0, and

harness pins no heading count — its own grammar line says the reconstructed arm prints every DECISIONS entry
